title: DR-LEF: Log-Euclidean SPD Riemannian Geometry and Calibrated Tsallis Entropic Discrepancy for Any-to-Any Multi-Spectral Object Re-Identification
summary: DR-LEF replaces binary-target orthogonality loss and unnormalized Euclidean triplet ratios in modality-decoupled multi-spectral ReID with Log-Euclidean SPD tangent-space orthogonality plus a calibrated Tsallis entropic discrepancy, reporting +3.2 mAP matched and +2.2 mAP mismatched on RGBNT201 (90.3 mAP with re-ranking) and +2.7/+5.7 mAP on MSVR310.

lessons.approach: Conformal Geodesic Cross-Ratio (CGCR) geometry in place of Log-Euclidean tangent orthogonality for covariance decoupling
lessons.error_summary: The paper reports CGCR collapses the query-gallery distance matrix's effective rank by about 74% (12.7 to 3.5), driving retrieval below 11% mAP, so the module was pruned. Voiculescu Free Entropy Alignment is also reported to yield no gain and leave shared-specific mutual information unchanged.
lessons.applies_when: Modality-decoupled multi-spectral ReID on RGBNT201 / MSVR310 with covariance-based orthogonality constraints

lessons.approach: Rigid binary (1.0/0.0) MSE orthogonality target (ROL) and unnormalized Euclidean covariance cross-correlation as the decoupling constraint
lessons.error_summary: On RGBNT201 the binary-MSE target reaches only 26.2 vs 37.2 mAP on mismatched+re-ranking relative to Log-Euclidean (21.0 vs 26.2 mismatch-average mAP), and the paper attributes this to dimensional collapse; a Cholesky tangent variant also does not transfer to mismatched settings (21.6 mAP).
lessons.applies_when: High-dimensional modality-decoupled feature spaces evaluated under query-gallery modality mismatch

lessons.approach: One loss-integration strategy for both object domains, and temperature or entropic-index settings outside the calibrated range
lessons.error_summary: No single integration wins: hybrid anchor retention beats pure replacement on deformable persons (75.6 vs 69.6% matched mAP) but loses on rigid vehicles (48.7 vs 50.9%). Temperature at or above 0.5 causes gradient starvation (57.6x smaller norm, CV 1.18), and the Shannon limit q=1.0 gives a peak gradient spike of 11577.74.
lessons.applies_when: Cross-domain multi-spectral ReID training with entropic discrepancy losses

lessons.question: How do I stop modality-decoupling losses from collapsing features and spiking gradients in multi-spectral re-identification?
lessons.answer: Enforce feature orthogonality in the Lie algebra tangent space of SPD covariance matrices instead of against binary scalar targets, and compute the discrepancy term on temperature-normalized probability simplexes. Matrix-log projection avoids rigid magnitude bounds (mismatch+re-ranking mAP 37.2 vs 28.4 for binary-MSE on RGBNT201), and calibrated Tsallis with temperature 0.05 and index 1.5 cuts gradient variance over 10x, gradient CV about 9x, and worst-case spikes about 25x.

lessons.question: Should a new geometric loss replace the baseline loss outright or be blended with it?
lessons.answer: Match the integration strategy to the rigidity of the target class rather than picking one globally. The paper found deformable targets need baseline anchors retained (persons, RGBNT201: 75.6 vs 69.6% matched mAP, intra-class variance 0.1031 vs 0.1736), while rigid targets do better with full replacement (vehicles, MSVR310: 50.9 vs 48.7% matched and 30.5 vs 28.1% mismatch, variance 0.1562 vs 0.2193).

title: SYMP-MONGE: Continuous Symplectic Contact Dynamics and Monge-Ampere Density Transport for Virtual Screening under Structural Uncertainty
summary: SYMP-MONGE adds a differentiable induced-fit contact flow, a symplectic sub-pocket hypergraph, a quaternionic spectral matcher and an entropic optimal-transport channel to a contrastive pocket-ligand retriever, reporting mean AUROC 0.9467, BEDROC 0.6532 and EF1% 40.17% on the 38-target DUD-E benchmark (vs 0.8734 / 0.6046 / 39.08% for AANet) at 8.05 s/epoch and 1.01 GB VRAM.

lessons.approach: Static-embedding hyperbolic dense retrieval (HypSeek) carried from co-crystallized holo pockets to blind AlphaFold2 structures
lessons.error_summary: The paper reports HypSeek is the strongest baseline on holo pockets (AUROC 0.956 / BEDROC 0.772 / EF1% 48.5 vs 0.955 / 0.738 / 47.2) but its crisp static pocket geometry does not survive structural uncertainty: EF1% drops 41.9 points moving to blind AlphaFold2 models, a 14.5 EF1%-point deficit on the five-setting average.
lessons.applies_when: Structure-based virtual screening evaluated on apo or AlphaFold2-predicted structures rather than holo complexes

lessons.approach: Geometric channels combined with a naive max-over-candidate-cavities aggregation under blind pocket detection
lessons.error_summary: The authors report an honest trade-off: under max-over-candidates the geometric channels slightly lower blind early enrichment (apo-pred blind BEDROC 0.6317 down to 0.5781) because a few spurious predicted cavities inflate the per-candidate maximum; a volume-penalized aggregation is reported to remove the artifact.
lessons.applies_when: Blind screening where pocket candidates come from a cavity detector with no co-crystallized ligand

lessons.approach: Transferring DUD-E contrastive-retrieval gains zero-shot to leakage-filtered random-real-molecule decoy pools (BayesBind, PLINDER)
lessons.error_summary: The fine-tuned heads do not lead on BayesBind (EFB1% 4.90 vs 9.45) or PLINDER, so the paper states the advantage is established only for property-matched screening under structural uncertainty; structural robustness still persists (delta AUROC under 0.02 across regimes).
lessons.applies_when: Evaluating screening models on random-real-molecule decoys instead of property-matched decoys

lessons.approach: Frozen projection heads, or unfreezing the whole transformer backbone, instead of end-to-end fine-tuning of tri-modal projections
lessons.error_summary: In the training-regime ablation over 20 DUD-E targets both frozen projections and full-backbone unfreezing underperform end-to-end tri-modal projection fine-tuning, which carries +0.1532 BEDROC over frozen heads; the frozen dual tower also collapses to AUROC about 0.30 on off-target cavities.
lessons.applies_when: Dual-tower contrastive screening models with pretrained pocket and ligand encoders

lessons.question: Why do contrastive virtual-screening retrievers collapse on apo or AlphaFold2 structures, and what fixes it?
lessons.answer: Replace static Euclidean pocket crops and binary IoU supervision with a differentiable ligand-conditioned contact flow and a soft entropic optimal-transport density match, and fine-tune the projection heads end to end. The paper reports this reopens collapsed cavities and gives detector-agnostic robustness, lifting AUROC by 0.006 to 0.010 per structural setting over an all-geometry-removed dual tower and reaching mean AUROC 0.9467 / EF1% 40.17% at negligible cost (8.05 vs 7.68 s/epoch).

lessons.question: Is it better to rely on one strong global contrastive similarity channel or to blend in localized physical channels?
lessons.answer: Blend them: the learned mixture of global contrastive and localized geometric channels is needed for early retrieval. The learned mixture reaches AUROC 0.9467 versus 0.9219 for top-2 channel truncation, with geometric channels (spectral, geo, OT, fine) summing to 52.1% of total weight against 47.9% for global contrastive channels, and the quaternionic-spectral channel alone (0.229) nearly matching the global cls channel (0.256).

title: Cellular Sheaf Harmonic Latent Alignment: Test-Time Prompt Robustness via Residual-Stream Topological Diffusion
summary: CS-HLA models a decision token's late residual-stream representation as a cochain on a cellular sheaf and applies a gated closed-form harmonic descent only when sheaf energy signals perturbation, reporting recovery of 72.8% of prompt-perturbation damage at +1.0% clean accuracy across 3 open-weight 7-8B LLMs and 10 tasks, at about 0.81 ms/prompt and no extra forward passes.

lessons.approach: Static residual-stream steering vectors (RepE, ITI, ActAdd) applied uniformly regardless of whether the prompt is perturbed
lessons.error_summary: Pooled over 3 models, 10 tasks and both perturbation families, RepE recovers none of the damage (0.0% recovery) and ActAdd barely helps, with the best steering baseline at 38.6% recovery versus 72.8% for the gated sheaf update; a logit-debiasing baseline reaches 61.6% recovery but costs -2.9% clean accuracy (-5 to -6.5% in format cells).
lessons.applies_when: Post-hoc test-time debiasing of prompt-format and typo sensitivity in 7-8B open-weight LLMs

lessons.approach: Putting the sheaf on full token-token context graphs (sequential, star, top-k attention, dense) with graph sheaf-Laplacian diffusion
lessons.error_summary: Every such topology yields negative recovery: best is the star graph at -9.6%, top-1 collapses clean accuracy to -24.5%, and the dense graph over-smooths at -77.1%. The paper reads this as the perturbation-relevant coboundary concentrating at the decision vertex, not in token-token interactions.
lessons.applies_when: Choosing the cell complex for residual-stream topological corrections

lessons.approach: Unsupervised restriction maps (identity, orthogonal Procrustes/SVD) for estimating the coboundary
lessons.error_summary: Both fail to capture directional shifts and give negative recovery (identity -44.9%, Procrustes/SVD -15.0%), while supervised coboundary fitting works (linear ridge 70.1% recovery at +1.0% clean). The paper concludes supervised fitting from a clean anchor set is essential.
lessons.applies_when: Fitting the restriction map offline from a small clean calibration set

lessons.approach: Running more than one harmonic-descent step per prompt
lessons.error_summary: Recovery peaks at a single step for all schedules; beyond three steps over-smoothing erases task signal and recovery collapses to negative values while clean accuracy drops, as kernel alignment with the zero-coboundary subspace rises monotonically (sheaf energy contracting at ratio about 0.886 per step).
lessons.applies_when: Iterating the closed-form latent correction at inference time

lessons.question: How can I make an LLM robust to prompt format and typo perturbations at test time without hurting clean accuracy or adding forward passes?
lessons.answer: Gate the intervention on a measured inconsistency signal so clean prompts are left untouched, and apply a single closed-form correction to the decision token's late residual stream. Treating that token's multi-layer representation as a cochain on a cellular sheaf, with an energy-divergence gate and one harmonic-descent step, recovers 72.8% of damage at +1.0% clean accuracy (damage up to 62.2% unmitigated), versus 38.6% for the best static steering baseline, at about 0.81 ms/prompt and zero extra forward passes.

lessons.question: Where in a transformer should a test-time robustness correction be applied, and how much capacity does it need?
lessons.answer: Concentrate it on the decision token across a few late decoder layers rather than spreading it over the sequence or the output logits. Late stalk depth beats early layers (early L/4 recovers only 47.7% on one 36-layer model), full token-token graphs give negative recovery, and edge-stalk rank compression saturates early: rank-64 factors store 6.35 MB (10.3% of full rank) and add 1.0 microsecond per prompt, with the isolated harmonic update at 0.059 microseconds.

title: HARMONIC-MoP: Harmonic-Preserving Spectral Decomposition and Dual-Context Prompting for Time Series Foundation Models
summary: HARMONIC-MoP adds harmonic-set-coherent frequency masking, a global-local spectral prompt router and a phase-aware dual-domain Fourier loss to a lightweight time-series foundation model, reporting a 40% cut in stage-1 reconstruction MSE (0.0198 vs 0.0329) and +3.1% MSE / +2.5% MAE zero-shot across the 7-dataset TSLib benchmark at 6.88M parameters.

lessons.approach: Masking only the fundamental peak frequencies during self-supervised pretraining, without their overtones
lessons.error_summary: Fundamental-peak-only masking scores 0.431 zero-shot MSE, worse than plain random frequency-bin masking (0.422) and contiguous-band masking (0.407), versus 0.387 for coherent harmonic-set masking. The paper reads peak-only being worse than random as evidence that masking fundamentals without overtones breaks phase lock.
lessons.applies_when: Frequency-domain masking objectives for time-series foundation-model pretraining

lessons.approach: Training with point-wise time-domain MSE only, dropping the phase-conscious dual-domain loss
lessons.error_summary: Removing H-Loss leaves stage-1 reconstruction MSE essentially unchanged (0.0197) but degrades zero-shot MSE to 0.420, worse than the 0.342 baseline and the 0.318 full model, because point-wise MSE permits arbitrary phase-shifted overtones. Magnitude-only (0.3952) and L2 (0.3695) variants also lose to joint complex L1 (0.3611).
lessons.applies_when: Zero-shot transfer to strongly periodic series after self-supervised pretraining

lessons.approach: Learnable or hard-adaptive spectral back-off and peak selection instead of fixed linear, entropy-conditioned soft masking
lessons.error_summary: Learnable back-off variants (exponential, sigmoid, threshold) add no gain on stochastic data yet regress on periodic data, and hard adaptive peak selection degrades transfer to 0.491 MSE through pre-train/tuning spectral mismatch, versus 0.409 for soft entropy-conditioned masking; added capacity does not help stochastic series such as ETTm1 and Weather.
lessons.applies_when: Adapting spectral masking strength across heterogeneous periodic and stochastic domains

lessons.approach: Scaling the harmonic tolerance band with window length, and assuming monotone benefits from more harmonic groups
lessons.error_summary: The MSE-optimal leakage tolerance is reported not to scale monotonically with sequence length: small fixed values stay near-optimal (tolerance 1 gives 0.387 vs 0.402) and inflating it at long lengths slightly hurts by over-masking non-harmonic content. The group-count sweep is also non-monotonic, optimal at 6 groups (0.387).
lessons.applies_when: Tuning DFT leakage tolerance and harmonic group count across window lengths

lessons.question: How should I mask frequencies and define the loss when pretraining a time-series foundation model for zero-shot transfer?
lessons.answer: Mask whole harmonic sets together, not independent frequency bins, and pair reconstruction with a magnitude-weighted complex Fourier penalty. Identifying top-K fundamental peaks with a small fixed leakage tolerance and masking their overtones coherently cuts stage-1 reconstruction MSE 40% (0.0198 vs 0.0329) for 9.8% epoch overhead (210s vs 191s), and the joint complex L1 loss turns that into +3.1% TSLib MSE and up to +10.1% on strongly periodic series.

lessons.question: How do I keep mixture-of-prompts routing stable across domain shift in a frozen-backbone forecaster?
lessons.answer: Condition expert selection on a sequence-level spectral signature as well as the local patch token, combined by multiplicative gating. The paper reports gated dual-context routing (0.466 MSE on ETTh1, frozen backbone) and global-only (0.464) edge out standard patch-token routing, and removing dual routing from the full model raises average MSE from 0.318 to 0.320; the benefit is reported as stabilizing which prompt a sequence's patches select rather than a large headline gain.

title: Soft-VSM: Threshold-Free Visual Consistency Evaluation for Subject-Driven Image Generation
summary: Soft-VSM replaces the hard semantic and visual thresholds of the VSM consistency metric with smooth confidence weighting and continuous integration, plus retraining of the feature networks, and reports oracle correlation of 0.638 linear / 0.674 rank versus 0.454/0.589 for pretrained VSM.

lessons.approach: Global image-embedding metrics (CLIP, DINO) and a VLM judge used to score localized visual consistency between reference and generated subject images
lessons.error_summary: Against a ground-truth inpainting oracle on 100 pairs, CLIP scored -0.052/-0.004 (linear/rank correlation), DINO 0.087/0.121 and the VLM 0.096/0.003. Masking the background did not help (masked CLIP stayed near zero), so the failure comes from spatial pooling, not background clutter.
lessons.applies_when: Evaluating fine-grained texture or logo consistency in subject-driven text-to-image generation

lessons.approach: Hard semantic gate Ts on point correspondences before scoring, raised from 0.6 to 0.8
lessons.error_summary: Correlation with the oracle collapsed from 0.652 to 0.533 as 66% of valid points were discarded (403.7 to 149.5 per pair). The thresholded metric was also about 4x more sensitive to the training loss balance alpha (0.679 to 0.728) than the soft version (0.635 to 0.647).
lessons.applies_when: Dense point-matching consistency metrics with binary confidence cutoffs

lessons.approach: Training the feature-disentanglement networks longer (14 epochs) and sharpening the visual score with a quadratic clamp
lessons.error_summary: Training loss kept falling but oracle correlation peaked at epoch 8 (0.638/0.674) and dropped to 0.575/0.649 at epoch 11 and 0.607/0.655 at epoch 14. A quadratic clamp on visual scores over-compressed mid-range values, dropping to 0.568/0.630. The paper notes the best checkpoint is fragile and needs ground-truth masks to pick.
lessons.applies_when: Retraining contrastive feature aggregators for an evaluation metric

lessons.question: How to make a dense visual-consistency metric robust without hand-tuned thresholds?
lessons.answer: Weight every matched point by a smooth confidence (for example ReLU(s)^2) and integrate the visual similarity over all thresholds instead of applying binary cutoffs. This gives a closed-form confidence-weighted score that matched the oracle-tuned best hard gate within 0.013 and reached 0.638/0.674 oracle correlation; it also transferred to human preferences on DreamBench++ with +0.101 linear correlation over standard VSM. Within smooth weightings the choice barely mattered (spread under 0.008).

title: Regularized Dual-Flow Routing with Value-Gated Feasibility Fallback for Budget-Constrained Multi-LLM Serving
summary: RDF-VG is a training-free online router across multiple LLMs that anchors on LP dual prices, paces them by real-time budget burn and gates fallbacks by net dual value, reporting 97.26% of the offline LP optimum on RouterBench (+11.27 points over PORT) at about 0.06 ms per decision.

lessons.approach: Static LP dual shadow prices learned on a warm-up sample (PORT-style) or periodic batch LP re-solving for routing queries across LLMs with token budgets
lessons.error_summary: Open-loop prices do not react to budget depletion; under 0.25x total budget PORT fell to 54.92% of the LP optimum and BatchSplit to 36.49%, versus 86.76% with closed-loop pacing. Myopic per-query routers exhaust top models early and push later hard queries to weak models.
lessons.applies_when: Online budget-constrained routing across heterogeneous LLMs with non-stationary output lengths

lessons.approach: Ungated fallback: when a query's preferred model is out of budget, send it to the best remaining affordable model
lessons.error_summary: Ungated fallback scored 2114.15 performance versus 2756.75 with no fallback at all on RouterBench, because it spent remaining budgets on low-value queries.
lessons.applies_when: Fallback routing after a primary model's token budget is exhausted

lessons.approach: Online dual-pacing learning rate set too high (eta >= 0.05), or disabled (eta = 0)
lessons.error_summary: With pacing disabled performance stayed capped below 2751.9; large step sizes (eta >= 0.05) degraded performance, while eta in [0.001, 0.01] was best (3217.2 even with no warm-up).
lessons.applies_when: Tuning online dual-price updates for budget pacing

lessons.question: How to route LLM queries under per-model token budgets without early budget exhaustion?
lessons.answer: Anchor on LP dual prices from a small warm-up set, then update them online in proportion to the real-time budget burn rate, and route to a fallback model only if its net dual utility (value minus price times cost) is non-negative. This reached 97.26% of the offline LP optimum on RouterBench and 116.66% on SPROUT, beat PORT by +11.27 and +39.84 points, and added under 0.3 ms per query end-to-end.

lessons.question: How to guard an online router against distribution shift without being over-conservative on clean data?
lessons.answer: Trigger time-uniform martingale confidence bounds only when neighbour distances or cost variance exceed historical tail thresholds, rather than applying them always. The paper reports this protects against capacity collapse under out-of-distribution prompts while avoiding clean-data conservatism; the method also kept 97.44% of optimum after shrinking the history repository from 26,497 to 5,000 records.

title: Procrustes-DS: Out-of-Distribution Detection via Class-Aware Layer Weighting and Asymmetric Log-Evidence Fusion
summary: Procrustes-DS is a training-free post-hoc OOD detector for fine-tuned ViTs combining class-aware layer weighting, scale-matched covariance shrinkage, a score-level off-manifold gate and weighted log-evidence fusion, reporting 99.56% AUROC and 2.17% FPR95 on CIFAR-100 versus 4.17% FPR95 for reproduced X-Maha.

lessons.approach: Fusing a class-covariance distance score and logit energy by unweighted addition or classical evidential (DS) mass fusion with sigmoid beliefs
lessons.error_summary: DS mass fusion was numerically identical to an unweighted sum (rank correlation 1.000000), both at 98.91% AUROC / 4.83% FPR95, worse than the distance score alone (99.07% / 4.28%). Weighted log-evidence fusion reached 99.56% / 2.17%.
lessons.applies_when: Combining multiple OOD scores post-hoc

lessons.approach: Empirical class covariance with no shrinkage, or a fixed-penalty precision regularizer, on fine-tuned ViT features
lessons.error_summary: After fine-tuning, feature variance shrinks to about 8e-4 per dimension and d=768 exceeds 500 samples per class, giving condition numbers above 1.4e4. No shrinkage dropped to 97.58% AUROC / 13.02% FPR95; a fixed penalty (about 0.0045 effective) far exceeds the true variance scale (~1e-4) and also fails.
lessons.applies_when: Covariance-based OOD scores on fine-tuned features where dimension exceeds per-class samples

lessons.approach: Class-blind layer weighting (uniform or total-variance trace) when mixing multi-layer features; feature-level gating of inputs
lessons.error_summary: Uniform weighting gave 99.32% AUROC / 3.30% FPR95 and 19.66% FPR95 on hard near-OOD CIFAR-10, versus 2.13% / 12.32% with class-scatter-ratio weighting. The paper reports feature-level masking distorts the geometry needed for near-OOD discrimination.
lessons.applies_when: Multi-layer feature-mixing OOD detectors on ViTs

lessons.approach: Applying the post-hoc detector to full fine-tuning or shallow visual prompt tuning instead of adapter-style PEFT
lessons.error_summary: The method still beat X-Maha, but absolute FPR95 rose to 22.21% with full fine-tuning and 11.79% with VPT-shallow, versus 2.17% with AdaptFormer.
lessons.applies_when: Post-hoc OOD detection across adaptation strategies

lessons.question: How to stabilize class-covariance OOD scores when fine-tuned features have tiny variance and few samples per class?
lessons.answer: Shrink the covariance toward its own scale, Sigma <- (1-s)Sigma + s(Tr(Sigma)/d)I, so regularization matches the feature variance with no tuned penalty. Combined with between/within class-scatter layer weighting and reliability-weighted log-evidence fusion, this reached 99.56% AUROC / 2.17% FPR95 on CIFAR-100 and cut FPR95 on near-OOD CIFAR-10 from 19.52% to 12.61%.

lessons.question: How to combine several OOD detection scores so the fusion beats the best single score?
lessons.answer: Standardize each score as log-evidence and add them with explicit per-source reliability weights, and apply safety gates only at the score level (an asymmetric min(0, z - theta) penalty for far-OOD). This gave 99.56% / 2.17% versus 98.91% / 4.83% for plain sum, and stayed above 99.41% AUROC across energy temperatures where energy alone fell to 79.87%.

title: Layer-Discounted RPB-ONOPT: Robust Learning-Augmented Paging via Work-Function Geometry
summary: LD-RPB-OM re-ranks predicted eviction candidates by their work-function layer depth and picks the discount strength online from shadow instances, keeping robustness guarantees and lowering mean cost ratio on SPEC CPU 2006 from 1.250 to 1.227 under the PLECO predictor.

lessons.approach: Fixed (non-adaptive) layer discount with a large scale gamma = 2.0 in learning-augmented paging
lessons.error_summary: Fixed discounting at gamma = 2.0 inflated cost ratio on POPU predictions (1.364 vs 1.349 baseline); the shadow-gated version stayed at or below RPB-OM in 25/25 grid cells.
lessons.applies_when: Layer-discounted eviction scoring with noisy next-arrival predictions

lessons.approach: Layer-discounted eviction evaluated on all SPEC CPU 2006 traces against RPB-OM
lessons.error_summary: Gains were modest and uneven: across 78 trace/budget pairs it got 30 wins, 29 ties and 19 losses, and under the POPU predictor it only matched RPB-OM (1.212).
lessons.applies_when: Comparing robust learning-augmented paging algorithms on real traces

lessons.approach: Windowed or per-set miss counters to choose the discount level online
lessons.error_summary: The paper reports windowed tracking reacts too noisily; global cumulative shadow gating gave the lowest mean cost ratio (1.381) and switch frequency (0.0021) on the ablation subset.
lessons.applies_when: Online selection among fixed-policy shadow caches

lessons.question: How to use noisy ML next-arrival predictions for cache eviction without losing robustness?
lessons.answer: Discount each candidate's predicted arrival by its work-function layer depth so lower-layer pages are evicted when predictions are close, and pick the discount level online by follow-the-leader over global cumulative misses of parallel shadow instances. This kept (Hk+O(1)) robustness and 1-consistency and lowered mean cost ratio from 1.250 to 1.227 under PLECO on 13 SPEC CPU 2006 traces.

lessons.question: How many discount levels does a shadow-gated online selector need?
lessons.answer: A small 3-level ladder {0, 0.3, 1} is enough: it matched dense 5- and 9-level ladders (cost ratio 1.3485 vs 1.3450) at 3x lower shadow-simulation cost across synthetic noise levels.

title: AWF-CP: Adaptive Whitened and Floor-Damped Feature Conformal Prediction
summary: AWF-CP normalizes feature-space conformal residuals with a covariance-whitened, floor-damped Jacobian sensitivity computed by one reverse-mode VJP, reporting 19.42% shorter bands than split conformal and 3.36% shorter than FFCP at 90% coverage across 11 regression datasets.

lessons.approach: Scaling feature conformal residuals by the raw Euclidean norm of the head's feature Jacobian (FFCP) on ReLU networks
lessons.error_summary: ReLU heads had about 50.25% exactly-dead Jacobian coordinates, causing gradient collapse and unstable, inflated bands; the isotropic norm also ignores feature anisotropy. Adding whitening and a floor gave +6.88% shorter bands on ReLU versus +2.26% (GELU) and +2.87% (Softplus).
lessons.applies_when: Gradient-scaled feature conformal prediction with piecewise-linear activations

lessons.approach: Split conformal prediction with uniform interval width
lessons.error_summary: Marginal coverage holds but conditional coverage does not: on MEPS19 it over-covered easy slices (~96%) and dropped to 48.9% on the hardest slice; mean worst-slice coverage was 65.96% versus 73.77% for AWF-CP.
lessons.applies_when: Regression intervals where difficulty varies across inputs

lessons.approach: Complex-step automatic differentiation or finite differences to get feature sensitivities
lessons.error_summary: Complex-step AD gave identical precision but was about 98x slower than one reverse-mode vector-Jacobian product, scaling as O(d) forward passes.
lessons.applies_when: Computing per-sample feature Jacobians for conformal normalization

lessons.question: How to get tighter input-adaptive conformal intervals from neural network features cheaply?
lessons.answer: Normalize residuals by a feature sensitivity that interpolates toward covariance whitening (rho) and adds a scale-proportional floor (lambda0), computed with one reverse-mode VJP, and pick layer, rho and lambda0 on calibration data with the plain FFCP setting inside the grid so it cannot do worse. This cut band length 19.42% versus split conformal and 3.36% versus FFCP at 90% coverage in sub-second runtime, and came within ~6% of CQR at over 1000x lower cost.

lessons.question: Do smooth activations remove the need for regularizing gradient-based conformal normalizers?
lessons.answer: Only partly: GELU and Softplus nearly eliminate dead gradients (0.04% and 0.23% vs 50.25% for ReLU), so the selected floor is lighter (0.160 and 0.069 vs 0.285), but whitening still gave +2.26% and +2.87% shorter bands over FFCP because metric anisotropy remains.

title: Stochastic Magnus-Bessel Tensor-Train Self-Consistency Bridges for Elliptic and Hypoelliptic Diffusions
summary: Proposes SMBTT-CCDB, a neural diffusion-bridge solver combining a Stochastic Magnus target operator, velocity-capped score guidance, curl-free potentials and a velocity-only projection, and reports it matches or beats self-consistency baselines on seven elliptic benchmarks while training up to 4.9x faster and solving hypoelliptic Langevin bridges where baselines reach infinite KL.

lessons.approach: Self-consistency bridge training with single-step backward Jacobian recursion (CCDB SC1) on steep potential barriers
lessons.error_summary: On 2D Mueller-Brown, CCDB SC1 failed with KL 67.57 and Max Energy +3.88 due to base-drift Jacobian explosion; without the auxiliary drift (eta=0) KL was 65.08 vs 28.69 with eta=1.0.
lessons.applies_when: Neural diffusion bridges via self-consistency drift control on potentials with high energy barriers

lessons.approach: Uncapped singular terminal score guidance ((T-t)^gamma + eps) for conditioning on a terminal point
lessons.error_summary: Near-terminal guiding velocity diverged (>2300 on Double Well, >10^7 on Mueller-Brown), giving 0/3 finite runs (100% NaN divergence).
lessons.applies_when: Doob h-transform style guidance as t approaches the terminal time T

lessons.approach: Unconstrained vector-field drift (ScoreMLP) or a soft curl penalty instead of a gradient-form parameterization
lessons.error_summary: Unconstrained ScoreMLP had relative curl 0.795 at d=100 versus ~1e-15 for exact potentials; an explicit curl penalty only reduced it to 0.126, violating the gradient-form fixed-point guarantee.
lessons.applies_when: Self-consistency bridge control that assumes u = grad(psi)

lessons.approach: Direct drift inversion with (sigma sigma^T)^-1 on hypoelliptic kinetic Langevin SDEs; also coupling the Poisson projection (lambda >= 1)
lessons.error_summary: Naive inversion injects drift into the un-actuated position channel, giving physically invalid paths and infinite KL; in the projection sweep, lambda >= 1 inflated velocity KL above the uncoupled value of 93.39.
lessons.applies_when: Bridges for SDEs where noise acts only on velocity (singular diffusion matrix)

lessons.question: How to stop neural diffusion bridge training from exploding near terminal time and on steep barriers?
lessons.answer: Cap the terminal guidance velocity and remove base-drift Jacobian compounding from the regression target. The paper uses a floored metric max(T-t, h_floor) with a saturating cap v_max*tanh(|f|/v_max) (v_max in [5,50] gave 0% NaN; v_max=25 gave 3/3 finite runs vs 0/3 uncapped) and an auxiliary drift b~ = -b, which cut Mueller-Brown KL from 65.08 to 28.69.

lessons.question: How to train a diffusion bridge for underdamped/kinetic Langevin dynamics with singular noise?
lessons.answer: Project control targets only into the actuated velocity channels instead of inverting the singular diffusion matrix. This Cotangent Bundle Poisson Projection kept dX = V dt exactly (zero position-drift error) with finite velocity KL, and trained about 3.7x faster (22s vs 79-83s) than trajectory-matching baselines; uncoupled projection (lambda=0) gave the lowest velocity KL.

title: CP-GRASSMANN: Counterfactual-Free Circuit Discovery via Flow-Matching Trajectories and CP-Tensor Factorization
summary: Proposes CP-GRASSMANN, a counterfactual-free neuron circuit discovery method using on-manifold path integration from retrieved contrastive anchors, and reports reaching faithfulness F >= 0.8 on Llama-3.1-8B subject-verb agreement with about 101 MLP neurons versus about 144 for RelP and 245 for Integrated Gradients.

lessons.approach: Higher-order CP-tensor synergy (rank R=5-20) and Grassmannian curvature metric (lambda 0.05-0.2) on top of first-order attribution
lessons.error_summary: On twohop and counterfact multi-hop benchmarks, neither gave a statistically significant reduction at operational budgets (p > 0.05); R>0 was a strict no-op for K >= 298 and no rank gave a faithfulness gain on counterfact. The authors recommend first-order attribution as the default.
lessons.applies_when: Neuron-level circuit discovery on Llama-3.1-8B multi-hop / factual-recall tasks

lessons.approach: Zero ablation (setting activations to 0) to evaluate discovered circuits
lessons.error_summary: Zero ablation pushed activations off-manifold, causing model collapse (millions of nodes needed for all methods) and near-zero faithfulness; dataset-mean and on-manifold anchor ablation preserved the method ranking.
lessons.applies_when: Evaluating circuit faithfulness in LLMs

lessons.approach: SVD-initialized PARAFAC decomposition at K=500 neurons, rank R>6
lessons.error_summary: SVD initialization materialized a dense K^2 x K^2 matrix needing about 500 GB of memory; switching to init=random reduced peak RAM to 0.30 GB.
lessons.applies_when: CP/PARAFAC factorization of large neuron-interaction gradient tensors

lessons.approach: Static contrastive anchor retrieval or difference-of-means anchors on unstructured tasks
lessons.error_summary: On open-domain Wikipedia generation, static retrieval degenerates since no opposite-class labels exist; flow-matching paths gave a 2x sparsity gain there. A diffmean anchor also needed more nodes on SVA (134 vs 101 at F >= 0.8).
lessons.applies_when: Counterfactual-free attribution baselines without clean opposite-class pairs

lessons.question: How to do circuit discovery in an LLM without hand-crafted counterfactual prompt pairs?
lessons.answer: Integrate gradients along an on-manifold path from a retrieved opposite-class contrastive anchor to the clean activation, instead of a straight line to a hand-made counterfactual. On Llama-3.1-8B SVA this reached F >= 0.8 with about 101 MLP neurons, on par with the paired-counterfactual upper bound (about 110) and sparser than RelP (144), IG (245), EAP-GP (308) and ACDC (388).

lessons.question: Which attribution path to use for structured vs unstructured tasks in circuit tracing?
lessons.answer: Use static contrastive anchors for templatic classification tasks and flow-matching-projected paths for open-ended generation. With clean near-minimal anchor pairs a single step (S=1) suffices; on unstructured Wikipedia next-token generation the flow-matching path gave about 2x sparser circuits. First-order attribution is reported as the sufficient default.

title: Differentially Private Empirical-Bayes Spectral Shrinkage Quasi-Newton Optimization
summary: Proposes DP-EBS-BB, a private quasi-Newton linear regression solver that reuses one privatized Hessian sketch across all iterations with Empirical-Bayes spectral shrinkage and risk-gated Huber clipping, and reports matching or beating AdaSSP, LinMix and IHM on 176 of 198 UCI privacy-dataset configurations and being strictly best on 168.

lessons.approach: Re-sketching the private Hessian at every iteration (T-fold composition) instead of reusing one sketch
lessons.error_summary: Per-iteration re-sketching forced higher noise per sketch and destroyed preconditioning quality; single-shot reuse matched or beat it on 32/36 configurations, winning all 24 ill-conditioned cells by up to 23.2% at epsilon=10.
lessons.applies_when: Differentially private second-order (sketched Newton) linear regression

lessons.approach: Exponential-mechanism quantile clipping, or under-clipping (C=10), for private gradients
lessons.error_summary: At epsilon=10 quantile clipping stalled at an accuracy floor 186x worse on 3D Road (1.43e-5 vs 7.68e-8) and 172x worse on Kin40K; on small datasets at epsilon=0.1, under-clipping amplified noise 6.3x.
lessons.applies_when: DP regression on large low-residual datasets (quantile) or small datasets (loose clipping)

lessons.approach: No preconditioning (P=I) or ungated Barzilai-Borwein step sizes in private quasi-Newton
lessons.error_summary: Removing preconditioning inflated risk by 2-6 orders of magnitude (Kin40K at epsilon=10: 4.5e4 vs 3.6e-7); ungated BB steps overshot and diverged under preconditioned noise.
lessons.applies_when: Private optimization on ill-conditioned regression problems

lessons.approach: Gradient tracking for noise suppression; static privacy budget splits; more iterations on well-conditioned data
lessons.error_summary: Gradient tracking alone barely changed parameter variance (1.01x) due to exponential lag; a static heavy-sketch split had 14.73x max regret on tall-skinny data vs 4.18x adaptive; well-conditioned Kin40K saturated near T=2 as gradient noise dominates.
lessons.applies_when: Tuning DP iterative solvers for linear regression

lessons.question: How to get second-order convergence in differentially private linear regression without paying privacy for every iteration?
lessons.answer: Privatize one Gaussian Hessian sketch at initialization and reuse it for all iterations, since reuse is free under DP post-processing. Pair it with a smooth Empirical-Bayes eigenvalue shrinkage preconditioner (matched or beat tuned ridge on 24/24 configs without tuning). Across 33 UCI datasets this matched or beat IHM on 176/198, AdaSSP on 177/198 and LinMix on 198/198 configurations.

lessons.question: How to reduce additive noise variance in private iterative optimization?
lessons.answer: Use Polyak-Ruppert iterate averaging rather than gradient tracking. It reduced parameter variance to a geometric-mean 0.55x of raw updates, lower in 18/18 cells, while gradient tracking alone gave 1.01x.

title: DR-COCO: Doubly Robust Co-Adaptive Verification for Efficient LLM Reasoning
summary: Proposes DR-COCO, which co-adapts a weak LLM verifier online from selectively queried strong-verifier labels using a doubly robust loss and non-monotone context features while keeping conformal Type-I/II error control, and reports a +0.080 matched-budget accuracy gain on Sudoku with 66% fewer strong verification calls and up to 37.7% lower calibration ECE on open-ended math streams.

lessons.approach: Naive online co-adaptation of a weak verifier using only strong labels observed when the policy defers
lessons.error_summary: Selective sampling bias concentrates feedback in ambiguous regions and starves confident tails, so naive updates fail to fix miscalibration and drift; DR-COCO cut ECE by up to 37.7% relative to it.
lessons.applies_when: Weak/strong verifier cascades where strong labels are only seen on deferred queries

lessons.approach: Pure inverse propensity weighting (IPW) without a baseline control variate for verifier updates
lessons.error_summary: On a miscalibrated MATH stream, pure IPW had extreme gradient variance (78.3) and destabilized calibration (ECE 0.178); adding a control-variate baseline plus clipping M=10 cut variance to 11.8 and ECE to 0.072.
lessons.applies_when: Off-policy learning from selectively observed labels

lessons.approach: Monotone score recalibration or monotone feature subsets to improve selection under quantile-tracking thresholds
lessons.error_summary: Monotone transforms leave candidate ordering unchanged (decision tau=1.000) and give no gain because the dynamic thresholds are quantile-invariant; only non-monotone context (consensus+entropy, AUC 0.872) helped (+0.014 on MATH Hard).
lessons.applies_when: Selective Strong Verification style accept/reject/defer with online quantile thresholds

lessons.approach: RKHS functional thresholds, dynamic exploration, fixed blending weight, and soft re-ranking on Sudoku
lessons.error_summary: RKHS boundaries stalled off-target (MAD 0.067, 150.6 us vs 0.010, 2.2 us scalar); dynamic exploration cost more than a static floor (1.55 vs 1.34 calls); fixed lambda=1 inflated cost 53% on Easy; Sudoku soft re-ranking alone gave -0.014 accuracy.
lessons.applies_when: Designing thresholds, exploration and blending for weak/strong verifier routing

lessons.question: How to learn a weak LLM verifier online from sparse strong-verifier feedback without biasing calibration?
lessons.answer: Use a doubly robust loss: weight observed strong labels by inverse selection probability, fill unobserved rounds with a baseline predictor, and clip propensities (M=10). This cut gradient variance 7x (78.3 to 11.8) and gave the lowest ECE (0.072), while scalar online conformal quantile tracking kept Type-I/II errors within targets.

lessons.question: Where do accuracy gains come from when cutting strong-verifier calls on constraint puzzles like Sudoku?
lessons.answer: A sound, zero-cost rejection filter (1-ply forward-check constraint propagation) gives most of the gain, not soft score blending. In a 2x2 factorial the free reject alone gave +0.079 accuracy at 0% false-positive rate while soft re-ranking alone gave -0.014; overall DR-COCO reported +0.080 matched-budget accuracy with 66% fewer strong calls.

title: Fisher Channel-Damped Engram: Curvature-Aware Closed-Form Machine Unlearning in Large Language Models
summary: Proposes a gradient-free closed-form unlearning editor that damps per-output-channel updates by a one-sided Fisher-ratio gate, reporting TOFU Overall 0.916 on Llama-3.2-1B (vs 0.851 for UCE) at about 30x fewer FLOPs than iterative gradient unlearning.

lessons.approach: Symmetric input-Fisher metric pullback weighting inside a pseudoinverse covariance projector for closed-form unlearning
lessons.error_summary: The pullback algebraically cancels inside the pseudoinverse and gave no gain; the earlier design carrying it scored 0.897 Overall vs 0.916 without it.
lessons.applies_when: Closed-form covariance-projection editors (UCE/LEACE/Engram style) on TOFU with Llama-3.2-1B

lessons.approach: Allowing the per-channel Fisher gate to amplify edits (Rmax > 1, or unbounded Rmax)
lessons.error_summary: Finite amplification mildly lowered Overall to 0.906-0.909; unbounded amplification was catastrophic (Overall 0.000). Attenuate-only (Rmax = 1) was best.
lessons.applies_when: Per-channel gated closed-form weight edits for LLM unlearning

lessons.approach: Computing reference covariance statistics on out-of-domain corpora (WikiText, C4, Alpaca) or question-only tokens
lessons.error_summary: Out-of-domain references collapsed the model (Overall 0.000); TOFU Retain90 halved it (0.378); question-only token statistics collapsed forgetting (0.302); all-tokens diluted to 0.818; pure SVD cutoff peaked at 0.846 and swung erratically.
lessons.applies_when: Closed-form unlearning where the total covariance must span the forget subspace

lessons.approach: Applying channel damping to MLP up/down projections or with uniform layer scaling
lessons.error_summary: Damping MLP up/down hurt (0.821 vs 0.903 for Q/K/gate only); under uniform layer scaling damping lowered Overall from 0.705 to 0.636.
lessons.applies_when: Layer targeting for closed-form LLM unlearning on TOFU

lessons.question: How to do closed-form, gradient-free unlearning of facts in an LLM without collateral damage?
lessons.answer: Gate the analytic weight update per output channel so it can only shrink edits on channels that matter for retained knowledge, never amplify them. The paper computes the gate from target vs reference Fisher curvature, uses answer-token statistics, in-domain references, a ridge penalty and adaptive layer scaling on Q, K and MLP-gate projections, and reports TOFU Overall 0.916 in 18 s, about 30x fewer FLOPs than iterative methods.

lessons.question: Does closed-form unlearning transfer to larger models and hazardous-knowledge removal?
lessons.answer: Keeping the gating hyperparameters fixed transferred reasonably across scale and tasks, though edit strength still needs per-scale tuning. The paper reports Overall 0.665-0.866 on 7B/8B models and 81% of MMLU utility retained on WMDP at matched forgetting vs 40% for plain covariance editing.

title: DiffTrop-Bitween: Differential-Algebraic Galois Reduction and Tropical-Idempotent Semiring Decomposition for Exact Randomized Self-Reduction Discovery
summary: Proposes a deterministic, LLM-free engine that finds randomized self-reductions using algebraic query orbits and exact rational null-space recovery, reporting coverage of 81% (65/80) on RSR-Bench vs 52% for a fixed-basis baseline.

lessons.approach: Floating-point regressors (Lasso, SVD thresholding, MILP sparse regression) to recover rational identity coefficients
lessons.error_summary: They missed 26%-46% of genuine identities; MILP reached 64.5% accuracy with 15.1% false positives at 387.9 s. Loosening SVD thresholds from 1e-12 to 1e-5 raised false positives from 13.2% to 29.1% without recovering any extra identity.
lessons.applies_when: Recovering high-degree rational coefficients of functional identities from sampled evaluations

lessons.approach: Relying on symbolic simplify() alone to verify candidate identities
lessons.error_summary: Symbolic simplification failed to reduce 94 of 334 genuine candidates (28% incompleteness), mainly inverse-trig addition laws and piecewise activations; one cube-root identity passed numeric checks but fails across the complex branch cut.
lessons.applies_when: Verifying discovered identities for transcendental and piecewise functions

lessons.approach: Exact rational recovery over the rationals under measurement noise
lessons.error_summary: Exact recovery held to noise sigma = 1e-8 but collapsed to 2.4% recovery at sigma = 1e-5, while total-least-squares SVD kept 69.3% at 1e-5 and 34.6% at 1e-3.
lessons.applies_when: Noisy black-box function evaluations

lessons.question: How to avoid floating-point false positives when discovering exact functional identities numerically?
lessons.answer: Snap null-space vectors to low-denominator rationals and discard any that do not rationalize cleanly, instead of tuning singular-value thresholds. The paper reports 100% recovery (189/189) with 2% false positives, and adds a differential-derivative certificate plus high-precision numeric checks to catch symbolic simplifier gaps.

lessons.question: How to find self-reductions for inverse transcendental or piecewise (ReLU, floor, abs) functions where fixed polynomial query bases fail?
lessons.answer: Generate query transformations from the function's governing differential equation (e.g. addition laws for arctan/arcsin) and add parity orbit columns f(x), f(-x) for piecewise functions. Combining these generators lifted coverage to 97% (29/30) on a stratified subset and 100% on piecewise benchmarks.

title: CHAMPS-RAG: Continuous Energy-Guided Attention Modulation and Hyperbolic Path Filtering for Zero-Latency Procedural Steering
summary: Proposes tag-free steering of reasoning models through standard operating procedures inside one forward pass (attention/logit biasing, hyperbolic progress tracking, particle beam steering), reporting a 91.1% macro-mean on four benchmarks with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, up to +5.2 points over TG-RAG at up to 8.9x lower latency.

lessons.approach: Entropy-aware adaptive gates that relax attention/logit steering during numeric emissions
lessons.error_summary: Gate variants were within 1.2 pp (inside seed noise); math accuracy came from math-aware stopping and self-consistency, not the gates, and the gates were a mild liability on Medical (best non-gated variant 96.0%).
lessons.applies_when: Steering a 14B reasoning model on Medical and GSM8K

lessons.approach: Dynamic recurrent edge synthesis (loop caps, convergence exits) for cyclic SOP workflows
lessons.error_summary: No accuracy benefit: plain DAG handling scored 95.3% vs 93.3% for full DRES (within noise) and no variant produced infinite loops; only frontier coverage rose (0.820 vs 0.807).
lessons.applies_when: Shallow cyclic diagnostic workflows with a well-behaved 14B backbone

lessons.approach: Binary hard fallback when the procedure graph is out of distribution
lessons.error_summary: Hard fallback gave a hallucination spike (2.0% vs 0.7%) and lower accuracy (91.0 vs 92.0) compared with soft density interpolation.
lessons.applies_when: OOD perturbations of procedure graphs in Medical domain

lessons.question: How to make an LLM follow a multi-step procedure without interrupting generation or injecting prompt text?
lessons.answer: Keep the procedure in persistent KV-cache reference blocks and steer with attention and logit biases while tracking progress from hidden states, rather than pausing on XML tags and injecting instructions. The paper reports 91.1% macro accuracy and up to 8.9x lower latency than interrupt-based baselines, and attributes most gains to tag-free tracking plus self-consistency selection.

lessons.question: How many particles or beams help for self-consistency style selection?
lessons.answer: Small particle counts suffice and the best count is task dependent. GSM8K accuracy scaled strongly up to K=4 particles while StrategyQA peaked at K=2.

title: Evolving Dual Information-Geometric Legendre Perturbation with Logit-Calibrated Dual Barycentric Consolidation
summary: Proposes forward-only post-training that samples Fisher-scaled weight perturbations, greedily selects specialists, and merges them into one model, reporting 81.7% on GSM8K for the ensemble on Qwen2.5-1.5B (+4.7 over isotropic random perturbation) and 73.0% for the single merged model.

lessons.approach: Exact dual-space perturbation mapped back by inverse logit transform
lessons.error_summary: Mean accuracy fell to 47.7% vs 61.0% for the weight-space approximation and 60.5% for isotropic noise; the inverse map distorts near-saturated coordinates and suppresses diversity.
lessons.applies_when: Random weight-perturbation search on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct

lessons.approach: Symmetric dual-Bregman divergence as a diversity term for specialist selection
lessons.error_summary: It correlated at r about 1.000 with Euclidean weight distance and selected identical subsets (59.67 mean both); greedy majority-vote selection itself gave the main boost (+1.33 over top-k).
lessons.applies_when: Specialists sampled around a single pretrained point

lessons.approach: Consolidating perturbed specialists into one model on a small high-curvature basin; also DARE-TIES merging
lessons.error_summary: On Qwen2.5-0.5B the barycenter collapsed on GSM8K to 7.0%; DARE-TIES collapsed to 6.1% mean on 1.5B. The merged 1.5B model also only tied naive model soup on mean (39.1 vs 40.7).
lessons.applies_when: Merging low-magnitude task vectors from derivative-free search

lessons.approach: Large perturbation scale sigma = 0.005 in random weight search
lessons.error_summary: Both the proposed sampler and isotropic RandOpt collapsed at sigma = 0.005.
lessons.applies_when: Perturbation search over 64-1000 candidates on 1.5B LLMs

lessons.question: Can LLM post-training be done with forward passes only, without gradients?
lessons.answer: Sampling weight perturbations around a pretrained model, scoring them on validation data and ensembling the best can beat gradient fine-tuning under small budgets. The paper reports 70.0% vs 44.0% for LoRA and 56.0% for MeZO at matched budget, 10.97 GiB peak VRAM vs 40.67 GiB for LoRA, and embarrassingly parallel evaluation.

lessons.question: How to choose a diverse ensemble of perturbed specialist models?
lessons.answer: Use forward-greedy selection on ensemble majority-vote accuracy rather than ranking candidates by individual accuracy. It gave +1.33 mean points over top-k on GSM8K/MATH/Countdown; output-disagreement diversity added a bit more (60.50) but was sensitive to its weight.

title: Topological Persistence Coherence Locking for Efficient Mixture-Model LLM Ensembling
summary: Proposes locking model switches in per-token mixture ensembling when persistent-homology distances on hidden states signal a reasoning transition, reporting +2.50 points on average over mixture ensembling (up to +16) at single-model throughput of 21-23.5 tokens/s.

lessons.approach: Monotonic quantile water-filling of logits (rate-distortion quantile alignment) across ensemble members
lessons.error_summary: It flattened output logits, raising decoding perplexity from 1.19 to 9.54 on math reasoning and collapsing accuracy.
lessons.applies_when: Token-level LLM ensembling of heterogeneous models

lessons.approach: Continuous linear-operator KV-cache extrapolation when switching models
lessons.error_summary: Dominated in both speed and fidelity by standard lazy KV prefilling.
lessons.applies_when: Switching active model mid-generation in mixture ensembling

lessons.approach: Static coherence lock on short knowledge multiple-choice tasks
lessons.error_summary: Locking caused regressions on knowledge tasks (e.g. MMLU 57 to 52, ARC 72 to 69 on one pair); no label-free competence signal beat explicit averaging on lopsided pairs.
lessons.applies_when: Short factual-retrieval MC tasks with one stronger and one weaker model

lessons.approach: Softening the hard lock to a probabilistic lock (0.7) or using small windows
lessons.error_summary: Soft locking dropped BBH from 78% to 66%; window w=4 over-locked into about 30-token blocks.
lessons.applies_when: Lock design for mixture-model ensembling

lessons.question: How to avoid reasoning derailment when an ensemble samples a different LLM at each token?
lessons.answer: Block model switching during detected reasoning transitions and let switches happen only when the hidden-state trajectory is stable, routed by an agreement-times-confidence competence score. The paper reports +2.50 points average over mixture ensembling, +8.4% on heterogeneous GSM8K (p < 1e-7), at 2-3x the speed of full-distribution ensemblers.

lessons.question: How to stop a reasoning-oriented decoding constraint from hurting factual QA?
lessons.answer: Relax the constraint whenever the model is confident (top-1 probability >= 0.90). This confidence gate removed the lock's knowledge-task regressions (MMLU 52 to 57, ARC 69 to 72) while keeping GSM8K, though BBH still favored the static lock.

title: InfoOptim: Format-Agnostic Scale-Space Weight Splitting and Hyperbolic State Companding for Memory-Efficient Training
summary: Proposes splitting master weights into a low-precision base plus integer correction and companding Adam states, reporting 50% parameter and 59% optimizer memory savings on GPT-2 124M with validation loss matching FP32 AdamW (4.4551 vs 4.4555).

lessons.approach: Pure linear quantization of Adam variance states
lessons.error_summary: Training diverged by step 101 because 93.1% of variance groups underflowed to zero.
lessons.applies_when: Low-bit optimizer states in GPT-2 pretraining

lessons.approach: Storing per-group variance scales in FP16
lessons.error_summary: Near-dead groups (variance about 1e-16) underflow the FP16 floor; a FP16-scale baseline underflowed a mean 0.212% (peak 0.507%) of live variance groups over 25k steps, vs 0.000% with FP32 scales.
lessons.applies_when: Compressed optimizer states with tiny-variance parameter groups

lessons.approach: Inverse-hyperbolic-sine companding for variance states
lessons.error_summary: Its linear near-zero region distorted small variances, worsening loss (5.5536 vs 5.5063 with square-root companding).
lessons.applies_when: Variance state compression

lessons.approach: IEEE 754 bit-shift master weight splitting on FP8 E4M3 weights; and dropping weight correction
lessons.error_summary: Bit-shifting raised a runtime error on FP8 (no scalar exponent fields). Omitting the correction term regressed loss (4.9925 vs 4.8592); INT8 correction recovered it (4.8570).
lessons.applies_when: Micro-scaled FP8 base parameters; master-weight elimination

lessons.question: How to drop FP32 master weights and compress optimizer states without hurting LLM pretraining?
lessons.answer: Keep a low-precision base weight plus an INT8 correction defined over the format's quantization cell width, compand momentum with tanh, and compand variance with square root plus an FP32 per-group scale. The paper reports matching FP32 loss over a 2.46B-token run with no downstream accuracy loss, and INT8 as the knee of the correction bit-width ladder.

lessons.question: How to recover step-time lost to optimizer state compression?
lessons.answer: Fuse the whole decompress-update-recompress optimizer step into a single kernel. The paper reports a 28.9x speedup over unfused execution (235.72 to 8.16 ms) with zero transient VRAM.

title: Scale-Invariant Robust Fenchel Tropical Attention for Out-of-Distribution Algorithmic Execution
summary: Proposes a max-plus attention with robust median-based scale normalization and clamping, reporting 77.09% mean Micro-F1 under value-shift OOD on 11 CLRS-style tasks vs 74.19% for softmax and 71.71% for prior tropical attention.

lessons.approach: Raw max-abs (unclamped) scale normalization in tropical attention
lessons.error_summary: Value-OOD F1 fell from 83.31% to 76.35%, the largest single degradation; max scaling inflated scale drift to 2.19x at 30% input noise and removing the clamp grew score variance about 3.1x.
lessons.applies_when: Max-plus attention under value-scale shift and input noise

lessons.approach: Unconditional devaluation (always on) or L2 normalization
lessons.error_summary: Unconditional devaluation blew up noisy regression MSE (0.019 to 0.064); L2 normalization stayed stable only by erasing cross-token contrast (-4.6 F1 under value OOD).
lessons.applies_when: Fractional knapsack and classification tasks in algorithmic execution

lessons.approach: Hard max-plus aggregation for smooth selection tasks; and raising Krylov rank
lessons.error_summary: Hard routing lost to smooth LogSumExp on Quickselect (92.18 vs 97.25). Increasing rank R from 1 to 4 raised latency 1.58x and memory 487 to 1284 MB with no value-OOD gain (58.29 vs 58.45); a second layer hurt noise OOD.
lessons.applies_when: Selection and transitive-closure tasks

lessons.question: How to make attention robust to input value-scale shifts in algorithmic reasoning?
lessons.answer: Normalize each sequence by a robust median-quantile scale with outlier clamping before scoring, rather than by the max or L2 norm. With median q=0.5 and clamp c=1 scale drift stayed at 1.07 at 15% noise, and Convex Hull value-OOD accuracy rose to 97.05% vs 68.95% for softmax.

lessons.question: Should attention use hard max routing or smooth aggregation?
lessons.answer: Use hard max routing for exact-geometry and dynamic-programming tasks and smooth LogSumExp for selection or noisy regression; a hybrid with one head of each recovers both. Hard routing led on Convex Hull (98.84) and all-pairs shortest path OOD (57.98) while LSE led on Quickselect (97.25).

title: Boundary-Weighted Adaptive Multi-Radius Submodular Cover for Sequential Data Selection
summary: Proposes a density-weighted multi-radius facility-location cover over train plus validation data for data selection, reporting the best curve-mean score (0.829 vs 0.825 bipartite coverage) across eight datasets and a 10.5-36x speedup via lazy greedy.

lessons.approach: Hard binary distance cutoffs or a single narrow kernel scale in coverage-based data selection
lessons.error_summary: Binary cutoffs reached 0.796 with 90.1% zero-gain greedy steps (early saturation); a single narrow scale collapsed to 0.722, vs 0.800 for a multi-scale ensemble.
lessons.applies_when: Greedy coverage surrogates for data selection on tabular benchmarks

lessons.approach: Modular (linear additive) selection objective instead of submodular aggregation
lessons.error_summary: Curvature 0 objective scored only 0.644 due to redundancy vs 0.791-0.807 with submodular aggregation.
lessons.applies_when: Data valuation where samples are redundant

lessons.approach: Ungated class-entropy boundary weighting
lessons.error_summary: Entropy correlated with within-class outlierness (rs = +0.360), front-loading noisy points and lowering score to 0.790; density typicality flipped this to rs = -0.998.
lessons.applies_when: Noisy datasets with near-flat class boundaries

lessons.approach: Stochastic greedy instead of lazy greedy for submodular maximization
lessons.error_summary: Marginally faster (0.022 vs 0.029 s) but lost exactness (Jaccard 0.276 vs selected set) and curve-mean (0.8107 vs 0.8135).
lessons.applies_when: Submodular data selection at small scale

lessons.question: How to select training data under a budget so early picks are not outliers and utility does not saturate?
lessons.answer: Use a facility-location cover over the joint train plus validation set with continuous multi-scale RBF kernels and within-class density-typicality weights, falling back to plain validation coverage when calibration says it is unsafe. The paper reports 8/8 wins over bipartite coverage (+3.0 pt early budget) and gains with ResNet-18/ViT features on CIFAR.

lessons.question: How to speed up greedy submodular selection without changing the result?
lessons.answer: Use lazy greedy evaluation of marginal gains. It needed 3,476 vs 125,250 evaluations (36x fewer, 10.5x faster) with identical objective value.

title: Query-Adaptive Monge Tangent Transfer for Multi-Source Distributional Regression in Wasserstein Space
summary: Proposes multi-source transfer for distribution-valued responses using non-negative simplex covariate weights plus query-adaptive references and soft source attention, reporting an 11.7% average prediction-risk reduction over the optimal-transport transfer baseline (WaTL) in 8 univariate regimes and up to 20.1% in 2-D.

lessons.approach: Raw unconstrained linear regression weights for multi-source distributional transfer
lessons.error_summary: Weights were negative on about 14.9% of query evaluations, producing invalid signed measures that need unstable post-hoc projection.
lessons.applies_when: Distribution-valued regression with queries away from the source mean

lessons.approach: Query-adaptive local reference barycenter in 1-D
lessons.error_summary: Reported as an honest negative result: in 1-D quantile space predictions are reference-invariant (bitwise identical), so the adaptive reference gave no gain; geometric stages were also non-significant under affine shifts.
lessons.applies_when: Univariate distribution responses or affine domain shift

lessons.approach: Sharp source attention temperature (tau = 0.1); dropping the directional tilt from weights
lessons.error_summary: Sharp selection was 21.2% worse than tau = 5.0; dropping the tilt (pure RKHS weights) raised mean RMSPR by 14.6%, erasing the advantage over the baseline.
lessons.applies_when: Multi-source transfer with dissimilar sources

lessons.approach: Query-adaptive transfer under extreme target scarcity
lessons.error_summary: With 16 or fewer target measures a non-transfer neural baseline and hard-selection AWaTL were marginally better because the adaptive barycenter itself is noisy.
lessons.applies_when: 2-D taxi drop-off and Eurostat transfer with very few target samples

lessons.question: How to avoid invalid negative weights when transferring distribution-valued regression across sources?
lessons.answer: Use exponential-tilting covariate weights normalized onto the probability simplex, so predictions are convex combinations of valid quantile functions. The paper attributes the 11.7% 1-D risk reduction to this stage alone and recommends it by itself for 1-D or affine settings.

lessons.question: When do geometric (local reference, tangent-space) transfer stages help for distribution regression?
lessons.answer: Only under non-linear multivariate transport; in 1-D they reduce to re-parameterizations. A dimension sweep found +8-13% over the simplex-weight stage for d in {2,3,5} (p < 0.05), with GPU optimal-transport solves keeping inference near 225 ms per query.

title: Loss-Aware Optimal-Transport Distributionally Robust Optimization with Amortized, Coverage-Calibrated Ambiguity Sets
summary: Proposes loss-aware OT-DRO that computes bootstrap transport distances in closed form in a linearized tangent space and sets the radius as a differentiable conformal quantile, reporting 30-50% lower out-of-sample regression error than trainable-OT DRO and about 880x faster distance computation.

lessons.approach: Learning the transport geometry while keeping the ambiguity radius frozen, or using a smooth coverage penalty
lessons.error_summary: Held-out coverage collapsed to 0.000 for frozen and penalty variants once the learned metric stretched distances (target 0.90); the penalty gradient saturates near zero. A straight-through variant reached only 0.859.
lessons.applies_when: Bilevel learning of OT cost in DRO regression

lessons.approach: Decision-focused DRO with frozen radius (DiffDRO) and split-conformal sizing (PtC) with small reference sets
lessons.error_summary: DiffDRO coverage fell to 0.645 on regression and 0.000 on a 10-asset portfolio; PtC under- or over-covered (0.714-0.999) with 20-30 reference samples.
lessons.applies_when: Portfolio and regression DRO with small reference sets

lessons.approach: Per-bootstrap optimal-transport linear programs inside bilevel OT-DRO
lessons.error_summary: About 551 s per instance vs 4.08 s for the closed-form tangent version (about 135x slower), with distance computation 819-881x slower.
lessons.applies_when: Bootstrap-calibrated OT-DRO

lessons.approach: Very small soft-quantile temperature for the differentiable radius
lessons.error_summary: Gradients exploded rather than vanished: variance 1.2e7 at tau = 1e-4 vs 7.1e3 at tau = 1.
lessons.applies_when: Differentiable conformal quantile layers

lessons.question: How to keep a coverage guarantee when learning the geometry of a DRO ambiguity set?
lessons.answer: Make the radius a differentiable conformal (1-beta) quantile of the bootstrap distances under the current geometry, instead of a fixed radius plus a coverage penalty. The paper reports this was the only method holding 0.90 coverage on all tasks (0.911-0.928) while matching the best decisions.

lessons.question: When does learning the transport cost in DRO pay off?
lessons.answer: When features include nuisance directions, a learned cost makes transport along them cheap and robustness budget is spent on decision-relevant directions. The improvement over isotropic OT-DRO grew from 6.61% to 22.01% as nuisance noise scale rose from 1 to 15.

title: Bulk-Restricted Total Variation Renyi-Dual DRO: Robust Decision-Making under Heavy Tails and Out-of-Sample Contamination
summary: Proposes a total-variation DRO over a calibrated data bulk with smooth CVaR and log-sum-exp envelopes, an extreme-value reach cap and a split-free coverage offset, reporting significant out-of-sample risk reductions over many DRO baselines across 100 replications and up to 49x speedups over exact solvers.

lessons.approach: Uncapped support extrapolation in TV-contamination DRO under large budgets
lessons.error_summary: Risk exploded linearly along heavy t-distributed tails (MSD 1016.5 at r = 20) vs 594.9 with an extreme-value return-level cap.
lessons.applies_when: Over-budget regimes (r > 10) with heavy-tailed losses

lessons.approach: Pointwise variance-based concentration bounds or uncalibrated quantiles to certify bulk coverage
lessons.error_summary: Pointwise bounds under-covered at scale (up to 20-21% failures at n = 5000-10000); uncalibrated quantiles failed in over half of replications.
lessons.applies_when: Bulk-set calibration with n from 200 to 10000

lessons.approach: Covariance-whitened distance as the bulk score on non-elliptical data
lessons.error_summary: On a bimodal t-distributed with an inter-mode gap anomaly, whitened-distance scoring collapsed to AUROC 0.255 vs 0.993 for Kernel-PCA.
lessons.applies_when: Multimodal or non-elliptical support

lessons.approach: KL / f-divergence DRO under heavy-tailed losses
lessons.error_summary: Divergence-ball baselines degraded sharply due to log-moment-generating-function instability.
lessons.applies_when: Heavy-tailed newsvendor and portfolio decisions

lessons.question: How to certify coverage of a data bulk set without wasting half the data on a calibration split?
lessons.answer: Use the maximum of a uniform CDF-deviation (DKW) offset and a variance-based offset on the scalar non-conformity score, computed on all training data. It gave zero coverage failures across n from 200 to 10000 and worked with any scorer, including Kernel-PCA and autoencoder scores.

lessons.question: Can smooth envelopes replace exact LP solvers in DRO training?
lessons.answer: Smooth log-sum-exp and softplus envelopes matched exact LP quality while being much faster and better behaved for gradients. MSD was 649.1 vs 647.8 at M = 2500, solve time fell from 14.06 s to 1.36 s, and gradient norms dropped from 5.958 to 0.148.

title: SpecAttn-Div: Spectral Cross-Attention Dispersal with Spherical Fidelity-Guarded Langevin Dynamics
summary: Proposes training-free optimization of the initial diffusion noise batch at t = T to spread attention layouts while staying on the noise norm sphere, reporting Vendi diversity gains of +0.04 to +0.18 on Stable Diffusion v1.4 with preserved CLIP alignment and about 3% overhead.

lessons.approach: Unconstrained Euclidean noisy-gradient updates of the initial noise seed
lessons.error_summary: Under aggressive dispersal the seed drifted off the norm shell (drift 9.79, aesthetic 4.856 vs 5.179); with K=10 steps drift reached +55.8 and diversity collapsed (Vendi 3.233 to 2.296) with aesthetic 4.814 to 3.456.
lessons.applies_when: Seed optimization for diversity in latent diffusion

lessons.approach: Cross-attention alignment hinge as the text-fidelity anchor at pure noise
lessons.error_summary: Forcing the hinge on did not help (ImageReward -0.979 vs -0.974 unanchored) because attention alignment at t = T is a noisy proxy; a CLIP score on the decoded clean estimate lifted it to -0.819.
lessons.applies_when: Aggressive latent dispersal on Stable Diffusion

lessons.approach: Exact tangent-space projection and injected noise as the source of benefit
lessons.error_summary: At K=1, simple Euclidean update plus post-hoc norm rescale matched the spherical tangent method; norm restoration was the operative ingredient and noise acted as a quality regularizer rather than the diversity engine.
lessons.applies_when: Single-step seed dispersal

lessons.question: How to increase diversity of diffusion samples without per-step guidance cost?
lessons.answer: Optimize the batch of initial noise seeds once at t = T to repel cross-attention query layouts from each other, and renormalize each seed back to its expected norm. The paper reports higher Vendi and recall with preserved CLIP at about 3% overhead, transfer to DiT-XL/2 and PixArt-alpha, and further gains when stacked with sampling-time guidance.

lessons.question: What anchor keeps text fidelity when perturbing diffusion initial noise?
lessons.answer: Anchor on an image-space score of the decoded clean estimate (CLIP similarity) rather than on attention alignment at pure noise. It raised ImageReward by +0.155 at high diversity (Vendi 3.073).

title: Flex-Dot: End-to-End Differentiable Operator Networks for Self-Extracting Concept Bottleneck Experts
summary: Proposes concept-bottleneck experts that each select one of six canonical formula templates via straight-through selection so the equation is read directly from the trained network, reporting 439x lower MSE than the distilled symbolic baseline and exact mechanism recovery on three of four benchmarks.

lessons.approach: Distilling a black-box task predictor offline with genetic-programming symbolic regression
lessons.error_summary: The distilled quotient c0/c1 gave 8644 test MSE from near-zero denominators; the pipeline is also slow and not faithful to the trained network.
lessons.applies_when: Symbolic mixture of concept bottleneck experts

lessons.approach: Unbounded division a/b in learned symbolic operators (also KAN reciprocal atoms)
lessons.error_summary: Test MSE 120 with 0.079% outliers on MNIST-Arithmetic vs 22 with bounded ab/(b^2+eps), eps = 1e-2; KAN symbolic snapping picked 1/x atoms and showed the same instability.
lessons.applies_when: Learned closed-form expressions with quotients

lessons.approach: Keeping a soft mixture over templates at inference instead of straight-through discretization
lessons.error_summary: The argmax read-out no longer matched the network: extraction gap 1.66 (dSprites) and 0.23 (Pendulum); a fixed near-greedy temperature caused premature lock-in, mis-selecting affine on Pendulum.
lessons.applies_when: Extracting equations from differentiable template mixtures

lessons.approach: MDL prior, L1 penalty and coactivation regularizers on expert templates
lessons.error_summary: Removing them changed test MAE by at most 0.02-0.06 and never changed template counts; they are not needed for the reported numbers.
lessons.applies_when: Template-based concept experts

lessons.question: How to get an interpretable closed-form task predictor from concepts without offline symbolic distillation?
lessons.answer: Make each expert a differentiable mixture over a small bank of complete formula templates and commit to one with an annealed straight-through selector, so the extracted equation is exactly what the network computes. The paper reports best accuracy among concept-transparent models on four benchmarks and expressions 2-5x more compact than a black-box mixture.

lessons.question: How many experts should a mixture of symbolic experts use?
lessons.answer: Match the expert count to the number of underlying mechanisms. MNIST-Arithmetic MAE fell from 8.61 (M=1) to 2.30 (M=4) and MAWPS from 4.68 to 1.00, while single-mechanism tasks needed only one expert.

title: Implicit Multi-Resolution Dual-Graph Verification for Decision Tree Ensembles
summary: Proposes an exact tree-ensemble verifier that lazily builds adjacency over a macro-cell hierarchy and searches it best-first with distance and class-feasibility bounds, reporting a median 95x memory reduction, 12.1x faster queries than in-RAM OC-Tree indexes and 100-400x faster than MILP.

lessons.approach: Explicitly materializing the output-configuration space in a spatial index
lessons.error_summary: Memory scales with the number of configurations; on 15 large models (more than 1e8 configurations) explicit enumeration failed outright, and any structural edit forces full re-enumeration (seconds vs sub-ms).
lessons.applies_when: Exact verification of large GBDT/random-forest ensembles

lessons.approach: Fixed macro-cell depth instead of adaptive refinement
lessons.error_summary: Fixed depths gave a U-shaped latency curve: coarse depth under-prunes, finest depth bloated memory 446-2,557x.
lessons.applies_when: Hierarchical lazy search for tree ensemble verification

lessons.approach: Constraint-solver (MILP) verification of tree ensembles
lessons.error_summary: 100-400x slower per query than the lazy spatial search and L-infinity only by construction, needing new formulations for L1/L2/hybrid norms.
lessons.applies_when: Robustness queries on tabular tree ensembles

lessons.question: How to verify robustness of large decision tree ensembles exactly without running out of memory?
lessons.answer: Generate the configuration-space graph lazily and search it best-first with combined spatial-distance and per-tree achievable-class bounds, keeping only the frontier in memory. The paper reports exact agreement on 1,065 ensembles, a median 95x memory reduction, and answers under 16 ms where explicit enumeration failed; compact arrays still win for tiny models (362 or fewer configurations).

lessons.question: How to update a verification index after pruning or adding trees?
lessons.answer: Refine only the affected macro-cells locally instead of rebuilding. Localized refinement was a median 20,918x (up to 50,705x) faster than full re-enumeration with exactness preserved.

title: Distributionally Robust Epistemic Risk-Optimal Conformal Prediction
summary: Proposes replacing the global worst-case loss in risk-optimal conformal decisions with worst-case risk over an adaptive KL ball around the predictive distribution, reporting realized loss 4.91 to 4.37 on BDD100K at alpha = 0.001 and 0.0% critical mistakes on a 10x medical loss matrix while keeping marginal coverage.

lessons.approach: Robustifying the in-set conformal quantile in addition to the out-of-set risk
lessons.error_summary: In-set robustification inflated thresholds and raised realized loss (2.790 vs 2.715 with out-of-set only), though it reduced critical mistakes separately.
lessons.applies_when: COVID-19 radiography decisions at alpha = 0.05

lessons.approach: Constant scalar KL radius, or removing the loss-tail floor
lessons.error_summary: A constant radius was inferior at every alpha; removing the floor collapsed the mean radius from 1.82 to 0.17 nats and raised high-alpha loss by 0.10.
lessons.applies_when: Adaptive ambiguity sets for conformal decision-making

lessons.approach: 1-Wasserstein (optimal transport), total-variation or chi-square ambiguity sets instead of KL
lessons.error_summary: W1 gave 3.84% critical mistakes vs 0.0% for KL on the 10x medical matrix; TV saturated on BDD100K; chi-square was 5.5x faster but weaker on safety.
lessons.applies_when: Heavy-tail-safe conformal risk control

lessons.approach: Risk-averse in-set calibration (RAC) and MC-Dropout base models
lessons.error_summary: RAC degraded to 12.95% critical mistakes and 9.36 realized loss on the 10x medical matrix; over-dispersed MC-Dropout degraded quality (2.977 vs 2.728 for a temperature stack).
lessons.applies_when: Safety-critical medical and driving decisions

lessons.question: How to turn conformal prediction sets into decisions without being over-conservative or brittle to a misspecified model?
lessons.answer: Hedge out-of-set risk with a worst case over a KL ball around the model's predictive distribution, with a radius that grows with predictive entropy and shrinks as alpha grows, plus a loss-tail floor. The 1-D dual solves in about 2 ms per query and split-conformal calibration keeps finite-sample coverage.

lessons.question: Does localized (per-bin) conformal calibration help decision quality?
lessons.answer: Yes at small alpha, but gate it to avoid small-sample over-coverage at larger alpha. At alpha = 0.01 it cut per-bin miscoverage spread from 0.0249 to 0.0013 and realized loss from 3.971 to 3.263.

title: Spatio-Temporal Disentangled Factored Recurrent Neural Networks for Neural Population Dynamics
