summary: Proposes ST-FacRNN, a factored low-rank RNN with a multi-lag, CKA-normalized temporal HSIC independence penalty and cross-trial pair pooling, reporting macaque M1 hand-trajectory alignment R2 of 0.802 vs 0.766 for FacRNN at K=4.

lessons.approach: Estimating the kernel Gram matrices per trial on short trials (T=14 bins) instead of pooling pairs across trials in the minibatch
lessons.error_summary: Per-trial Gram estimation gave lower alignment (0.748 vs 0.772) and was slower (6.41 vs 4.24 s/epoch); the paper reports per-trial unnormalized kernels on short sequences are ill-conditioned and prone to latent subspace collapse.
lessons.applies_when: Kernel independence penalties (HSIC/CKA) on short neural recording trials, macaque M1 reaching data

lessons.approach: Using only one regularizer for sub-circuit disentanglement: pure instantaneous partial-correlation penalty or pure temporal HSIC penalty
lessons.error_summary: Pure PC (beta=20) restored static independence (0.129) but not dynamic cross-talk; pure t-HSIC (beta=5) improved trajectory recovery (0.846) but left static bias (PC 0.569). Unregularized models failed outright (group R2 0.630, PC 0.874). Only the combination reached PC 0.126 and R2 0.887.
lessons.applies_when: Factored low-rank RNN/VAE models of neural population dynamics, synthetic Lorenz-Thomas data

lessons.approach: Widening the temporal lag window of the independence penalty to plus/minus 4 steps
lessons.error_summary: The +/-4 lag window regressed monkey alignment to 0.763 (vs 0.802 at +/-2) at the highest compute cost; instantaneous-only (lag 0) was weakest at 0.772.
lessons.applies_when: Temporal HSIC disentanglement on short trial sequences

lessons.question: How to disentangle latent sub-circuits in RNN models of neural data without time-lagged cross-talk?
lessons.answer: Penalize dependence between latent groups at small time lags as well as instantaneously, with normalized kernels pooled across trials. ST-FacRNN combines a partial-correlation penalty with a CKA-normalized HSIC over lags -2..2, reporting M1 alignment R2 0.802 vs 0.766 and synthetic connectivity R2 0.783 vs 0.771, while matching CEBRA/LFADS/PSID on decoding.

title: SAVVY-Vortex: Robust Multimodal Spatial Reasoning via Circular Orientation Pooling, Anisotropic Precision Tracking, and Boundary Soft-Margin Decoding
summary: Proposes a training-free geometric plugin (circular orientation pooling, precision-weighted trajectory fusion, soft-margin sector decoding) for audio-visual spatial QA, reporting 57.6% overall accuracy on SAVVY-Bench vs 56.3% for the reproduced baseline.

lessons.approach: Pooling per-frame orientation angles with a naive linear mean (no wrap-around handling)
lessons.error_summary: Linear-mean orientation pooling collapsed allocentric-direction accuracy to 41.7% with 62.6 degree mean angular error, below the circular (von Mises style) pooling result of 46.2%.
lessons.applies_when: Estimating facing directions from frame-wise angles near +/-180 degrees, 602 allocentric-direction samples

lessons.approach: Soft Gaussian voting across sector boundaries for egocentric direction answers
lessons.error_summary: Soft-margin voting hurt egocentric direction near boundaries (63.5% to 59.4%); the hard point estimate was best (84.7%), and for allocentric direction soft and hard decoding tied at 46.2%.
lessons.applies_when: Converting continuous direction estimates into categorical sectors when the point estimate is already accurate

lessons.approach: Adding a downstream box moving-average smoother after precision-weighted trajectory fusion
lessons.error_summary: Box windows dropped overall accuracy to 56.5% (-1.1); losses concentrated on low-curvature static tracks (56.3% to 54.8%). An RTS Kalman smoother added only +0.1, so no smoother was shipped.
lessons.applies_when: Trajectory pipelines that already smooth upstream

lessons.approach: Using raw segmentation confidence as a visual reliability weight, or recovering low-confidence detections unweighted
lessons.error_summary: Detector confidence correlated near zero with localization error (r=-0.019); naively recovering sub-threshold frames unweighted collapsed QA accuracy to 42.3%. Optical-flow jitter was predictive (r=0.357) and weighting by it cut error by 0.506 m.
lessons.applies_when: Visual-only tracking with monocular depth masks

lessons.question: How to fuse noisy visual depth and spatial-audio tracks for 3D spatial question answering?
lessons.answer: Weight each frame by an explicit inverse-variance model (depth error growing with range squared, audio confidence from coherent-to-diffuse ratio) and pool angles with circular statistics. Training-free, this gave 57.6% vs 56.3% on SAVVY-Bench (p=0.0024), egocentric distance 60.6% vs 58.8%, and 82.0% on Ego3D-Bench.

title: Polar-Geodesic Phase-Consistent Cross-Domain Integrated Gradients
summary: Proposes PG-CDIG, which integrates attributions along polar magnitude/phase geodesics with a phase-complete score Re(s)+lambda|Im(s)|, reporting better CPD faithfulness than baselines in 10/10 settings across five time-series datasets.

lessons.approach: Cartesian straight-line interpolation of complex Fourier/STFT features in cross-domain integrated gradients
lessons.error_summary: When target and baseline phases oppose, the straight path passes near the origin, dropping mid-path magnitude toward zero and producing out-of-distribution gradient spikes; mid-path spectral energy preservation was 0.959 vs 1.000 for the polar path.
lessons.applies_when: Attribution in complex transform domains (DFT, STFT, CWT) for time-series classifiers

lessons.approach: Fusing real and imaginary attribution components with nonlinear rules such as the Euclidean magnitude
lessons.error_summary: Nonlinear fusions distorted the sign of the completeness-preserving real term and degraded faithfulness; the absolute linear sum Re(s)+lambda|Im(s)| was best under both protocols on Boiler.
lessons.applies_when: Combining complex-valued Wirtinger sensitivities into a single importance score

lessons.question: How to compute faithful feature attributions for models operating on Fourier or wavelet features?
lessons.answer: Include phase sensitivity in the attribution score rather than only the real (magnitude) part. Adding lambda|Im(s)| improved CPD over magnitude-only CDIG in 4/4 settings and 6/6 transform settings; a 2x2 factorial attributed most gain to the phase term (+0.086 to +0.123 CPD), with the polar path secondary.

lessons.question: How many quadrature steps does path-integrated attribution need?
lessons.answer: About 20 integration steps are enough for path-based attribution in this setting. CPD converged by K=20 (within 0.4-3.3% of K=100) at a 5x speedup (14.9 vs 74.4 ms per sample on PAM).

title: Mem-MaxRL: Memory-Augmented Maximum Likelihood Reinforcement Learning for Preventing Coverage Collapse in LLM Reasoning
summary: Proposes Mem-MaxRL, which adds an EMA-smoothed pass-rate weight and a per-prompt success buffer replayed during all-fail deadlocks to maximum-likelihood RL, reporting 66.4% pass@256 on a 17x17 maze task vs 59.4% base and 25.8% for MaxRL.

lessons.approach: Expected-reward RLVR objectives (GRPO, RLOO) and plain maximum-likelihood RL trained with 32 rollouts per prompt
lessons.error_summary: All collapsed multi-sample coverage far below the pretrained base (pass@256 59.4%): GRPO 17.2%, RLOO 20.3%, MaxRL 25.8%; coverage optimizers SimKO 26.5%, PKPO 37.5% and replay baseline RLEP 28.3% also fell below base.
lessons.applies_when: RL with binary correctness rewards on a recurring 256-prompt maze reasoning benchmark

lessons.approach: Replaying semantically retrieved successful trajectories from other prompts without re-verifying them on the target prompt
lessons.error_summary: Only 0.14% of retrieved completions solved the target maze; 24,761 false-positive updates collapsed pass@256 to 7.8% (-51.6 vs base). Re-verifying with the reward function raised precision to 100% and pass@256 to 68.0%.
lessons.applies_when: Cross-prompt memory replay in RL on non-recurring prompt streams (25,600 unique mazes)

lessons.approach: Exact-match per-prompt success memory when prompts never recur
lessons.error_summary: Exact-match memory rescued 0% of all-fail deadlocks on a fully non-recurring stream, degrading to the smoothed MaxRL baseline; dense or cluster retrieval restored rescue to about 99.7%.
lessons.applies_when: Streaming RL training where each prompt appears once

lessons.approach: Optimizing pure Mem-MaxRL for coverage
lessons.error_summary: The coverage objective trades away some single-sample accuracy (about 0.4 points of pass@1 on Qwen2.5-3B); a hybrid loss mixed with GRPO was needed to recover pass@1.
lessons.applies_when: Qwen2.5-3B on GSM8K/MATH-500 when pass@1 matters

lessons.question: How to stop RL fine-tuning of LLM reasoners from collapsing pass@k coverage?
lessons.answer: Store verified successes per prompt and replay one with a clipped update whenever all rollouts fail, and smooth the 1/p weight with an EMA. This converted up to 22 otherwise-wasted all-fail prompts per step into updates, giving 66.4% pass@256 vs 59.4% base and 31.8% pass@16 vs 12.7% for MaxRL.

title: VD-STrans: Ultra-Low-Latency Incremental Byte Pair Encoding via Vectorized Direct-Interval Suffix Transduction
summary: Proposes VD-STrans, which flattens the small suffix-successor trees of BPE vocabularies into 256-bit vectors searched with branchless AVX2, reporting a 1.123x geomean (up to 1.271x) speedup over the best incremental BPE with exact fidelity.

lessons.approach: Raising the tree-flattening cutoff K beyond 8 nodes (K=16, K=32) to cover more vocabulary trees
lessons.error_summary: Coverage rose only marginally (99.88%, 99.97% vs 99.19%) while geomean throughput fell from 28.44 to 27.22 and 26.55 MiB/s because of multi-register scanning on every search.
lessons.applies_when: SIMD-flattened search structures for BPE tokenizers across 12 tokenizers

lessons.approach: Using AVX-512 instead of AVX2 for the decision kernel
lessons.error_summary: AVX-512 gave no advantage over AVX2 (2.58 ns) because trees rarely exceed 8 lanes.
lessons.applies_when: Small fixed-size search trees (<= 8 nodes)

lessons.approach: Branchy scalar search and linear scans as the search kernel or deep-tree fallback
lessons.error_summary: Under adversarial unpredictable inputs in L2, branchy scalar latency rose 68% (5.82 to 9.76 ns); linear scans beat a centroid search tree only for shallow trees and lost beyond about 96 nodes.
lessons.applies_when: Tokenizer search kernels on adversarial or deep-tree inputs

lessons.question: How to speed up incremental BPE tokenization on CPUs?
lessons.answer: Flatten small pointer-based trees into contiguous fixed-width vectors and search them branchlessly, keeping a logarithmic fallback for rare deep trees. Flattening alone gave 1.128x, AVX2 1.009x and an atomic single-byte fast path 1.051x, stacking to 1.197x in the component ablation, with 100% exact output.

title: Koopman-DMD: Latent Spectral Steering and Dynamical Mode Control for Parallel LLM Inference
summary: Proposes a training-free controller that models hidden-state trajectories of parallel shared-KV-cache workers with streaming DMD and damps transient modes, reporting a +0.0556 mean accuracy gain over the 2-worker baseline on LIMO with QwQ-32B at about 5% latency overhead.

lessons.approach: Replacing RoPE key rotations with Koopman-extrapolated cross-worker keys in a frozen model
lessons.error_summary: Direct key-vector substitution caused severe reasoning collapse: frozen query/key projections expect exact RoPE-rotated keys, so changed norms and phases destroyed attention. Steering was moved to residual-stream projections instead.
lessons.applies_when: Training-free intervention on frozen transformer attention

lessons.approach: Static activation steering (ActAdd/CAA) and budget-matched self-consistency voting as alternatives for parallel reasoning
lessons.error_summary: Static ActAdd/CAA degraded accuracy (0.2986 vs 0.3125 baseline): a fixed steering direction distorts valid reasoning when the worker is not over-thinking. Self-consistency also failed to beat the baseline under matched compute.
lessons.applies_when: Frozen QwQ-32B on LIMO and MATH-500 math reasoning

lessons.approach: Constant (not budget-relaxed) damping, uniform attenuation of all modes, or damping persistent modes
lessons.error_summary: Constant damping matched gains at 512/1024 steps but regressed at 2048 (0.4792 vs 0.4896); uniform attenuation cost -0.0125; damping persistent modes collapsed accuracy to 0.0833.
lessons.applies_when: Spectral damping of hidden-state modes during long generation

lessons.approach: Higher truncation rank (r >= 8) in streaming DMD of hidden states
lessons.error_summary: Higher ranks absorbed activation noise, exploding the condition number (> 1e5 at r=12) and lowering accuracy to 49.3% vs 52.08% at r=6; r <= 4 under-fit (48.6%).
lessons.applies_when: Online DMD over transformer residual activations

lessons.question: How to steer LLM reasoning without hurting it when the model is not drifting?
lessons.answer: Use closed-loop, state-dependent steering that intervenes only when a drift signal is detected, applied in the residual stream. Damping only fast-decaying transient DMD modes gave +0.0556 mean accuracy over the baseline on LIMO, +0.0606 on MATH-500 and +0.1000 on AIME-2024, and lowered perplexity (1.402 to 1.321).

title: Canonical Resonant Koopman Spectral Flow for Scalable and Stabilized Language Model Reasoning
summary: Proposes ResoKoopman, a controller on a frozen LLM whose latent generator is block-diagonal 2x2 damped rotations integrated in closed form, reporting 50.87% greedy@1 and 61.87% maj@8 on GSM8K with Llama-3.2-3B at about 6% latency overhead.

lessons.approach: Allowing unconstrained (possibly negative) damping rates in the latent linear dynamics
lessons.error_summary: Removing the softplus floor admitted negative damping, causing exponential mode growth and NaN divergence (0.00% accuracy on a 300-example subset).
lessons.applies_when: Continuous-time latent controllers with learned eigenvalues

lessons.approach: Ablating the rotation or decay part of the 2x2 blocks (pure dissipative or pure rotational dynamics)
lessons.error_summary: Pure dissipative (no rotation) dropped greedy@1 from 52.00% to 50.67% and expanded state norms 13x; pure rotational (no decay) lowered maj@8 by 4.00 points to 57.67%.
lessons.applies_when: GSM8K 300-example ablation with frozen Llama-3.2-3B

lessons.approach: Constant (ungated) injection of controller output when the top decoder layers are co-adapted
lessons.error_summary: Constant injection wins narrowly on a frozen base but degraded a top-2-layer co-adapted base by 3.26%, while the dynamic gate gave +2.20%.
lessons.applies_when: Fine-tuning upper layers jointly with a steering controller

lessons.question: How to add a stable continuous latent memory to a frozen LLM cheaply?
lessons.answer: Parameterize the latent linear dynamics as decoupled 2x2 damped-rotation blocks with damping forced non-negative, so the exponential is closed form and contractive. This runs in linear time, adds 1.72 ms/token (+5.9%) vs about 2.3x for latent chain-of-thought methods, and reports +3.18 maj@8 over a prior controller on GSM8K.

title: Conformal Implicit Quantile Steering Policy Control: Non-Asymptotic Safety Guarantees for Generative Models
summary: Proposes CIQS-PC, conformal risk control with per-prompt thresholds from an implicit quantile generator gated by a context-safety predictor, reporting 100% empirical FDR control on MedLFQA with subclaim recall +0.037 over generalized conformal risk control.

lessons.approach: Random per-prompt threshold dispersion as a way to raise recall under conformal FDR control
lessons.error_summary: Random dispersion smooths the step-shaped risk curve (+0.0458 recall) but treats risky and safe prompts alike; on single-claim prompts, where FDR is binary, it gained only +0.035 vs +0.251 for a learned safety gate, and is not conditionally safe.
lessons.applies_when: Conformal risk control of LLM long-form medical answers (MedLFQA)

lessons.approach: Fixed uniform threshold grids for calibration with peaked scores (log-probabilities, frequency)
lessons.error_summary: Uniform grids put almost no candidates in the high-confidence band near 1 and starved low-alpha recall to 0.0; placing candidates at empirical breakpoints fixed this at lower cost.
lessons.applies_when: Threshold search in conformal calibration with concentrated score distributions

lessons.approach: Relying on a single global threshold (generalized conformal risk control)
lessons.error_summary: A global scalar settles on a staircase jump of the discrete FDR loss, leaving unused risk budget (FDR slack 0.0030 vs 0.0009 with dispersion) and lower recall.
lessons.applies_when: Heterogeneous prompts with coarse per-prompt loss

lessons.question: How to raise utility of conformal FDR control for LLM outputs without losing the guarantee?
lessons.answer: Use per-context thresholds driven by a learned context-safety predictor, keeping the guarantee from the calibration step itself. The learned gate (correlation +0.424 with true cleanliness) lifted recall +0.0708 over the global threshold while FDR control held at 100% across 50 trials; a linear gate was the best cost/benefit choice.

title: Sheaf-Diffusion Tsallis-Entropy Toda-Lattice Compression: Efficient Single-Pass Non-Backpropagation Learning
summary: Proposes SD-TTC, a label-free layer-wise learning rule that synthesizes noisy variations by diffusion in hidden space after one forward pass and uses a scale-invariant dimensionality metric, reporting 77.50% vs 76.96% on CIFAR-10 with 3.3-4.2x faster training and about 20x fewer FLOPs.

lessons.approach: Measuring effective dimensionality with an uncentered second moment in dimensionality-compression local learning
lessons.error_summary: The magnitude-sensitive metric cost -1.68 points on CIFAR-10 in drop-one-out and over-sparsified activations (sparseness 0.39 to 0.56); the abstract reports about +10 points for the scale-invariant metric in a separate comparison.
lessons.applies_when: Unsupervised effective-dimensionality objectives for layer-wise training of convnets

lessons.approach: A constant compression weight shared by all samples and layers
lessons.error_summary: A constant weight over-compressed at large alpha and had to be tuned per dataset; the per-sample spectral-gap gate tracked the best constant without tuning.
lessons.applies_when: Compression-vs-expansion local learning objectives across datasets

lessons.approach: Label-free local layer-wise learning compared with end-to-end backpropagation
lessons.error_summary: Accuracy still trails backpropagation and equilibrium-based learning on the hardest datasets; scaling to ImageNet-1K and transformers was not shown.
lessons.applies_when: CIFAR-100, STL-10, Tiny-ImageNet with block-wise ResNet-18

lessons.question: How to make noise-based local (non-backprop) learning cheaper?
lessons.answer: Generate the noisy within-sample variations in hidden space from one forward pass instead of running many stochastic forward passes. Sheaf-Laplacian diffusion gave a 4.2x phase-1 speedup with up to 14x less memory and about 20x fewer FLOPs, while accuracy matched or beat the multi-pass baseline (54.55 vs 53.29 on CIFAR-100).

title: Amortized Nullspace Stiefel Embedding with Diffeomorphic Log-Barrier Flow for Hard-Constrained Deep Learning
summary: Proposes ANSE, a hard-constrained network that parameterizes outputs in the equality-constraint nullspace, runs equilibrated splitting in the reduced space and polishes with a log-barrier flow, reporting 2.9-3.2x faster training than the lifted-space baseline and machine-precision constraint violation on DC3 QPs.

lessons.approach: Soft constraint penalties (lambda=10, 100) or a hypernetwork that learns an approximate nullspace basis
lessons.error_summary: Soft penalties failed entirely (constraint violation > 1, 0% feasible); the learned hypernetwork basis only approximately spans the nullspace, giving equality violation 0.38 and 0% feasibility vs 1.9e-14 and 100% for the exact basis.
lessons.applies_when: Neural networks that must output solutions satisfying equality constraints, DC3 non-convex QP benchmark

lessons.approach: Truncating the projection/splitting iterations at test time without a feasibility polishing step
lessons.error_summary: Without the barrier polish, aggressive truncation was 0% feasible; the lifted-space baseline was 0% feasible for test budgets <= 50 iterations and only recovered at 200.
lessons.applies_when: Low-latency inference with iterative projection layers

lessons.approach: Running reduced-space splitting without row equilibration
lessons.error_summary: The unequilibrated operator (condition number 12.99) stalled at constraint violation 3.3e-3 with 98.5% feasibility at K=200; unit-norm row scaling dropped it to 2.13 and gave 100% feasibility.
lessons.applies_when: Douglas-Rachford style splitting with a fixed step size

lessons.approach: Deflated or recycled Krylov solvers and high-k GMRES for the implicit backward pass
lessons.error_summary: These cost 10.8-13.0 ms for no accuracy gain over plain BiCGSTAB (k=25), which was essentially exact (rel-L2 2.4e-10) in 4.9 ms.
lessons.applies_when: Well-conditioned reduced-space adjoint solves

lessons.question: How to make a neural network satisfy linear equality constraints exactly?
lessons.answer: Parameterize the output as a particular solution plus an orthonormal nullspace basis times free variables, so equalities hold by construction. This gave equality violation about 1e-14 with no forward factorizations, 2.9-3.2x faster training than the lifted-space baseline and 100% feasibility on QPs up to d=1000; it assumes a static constraint matrix.

title: Continuous Optimal-Transport Flow Matching & Spectral Information-Bottleneck for Anti-Causal Representation Learning
summary: Proposes COFM-SIB, combining one-step optimal-transport flow matching for counterfactuals, sliced-Wasserstein environment alignment, an RFF-HSIC bottleneck and task-shielded gradient projection, reporting 88.65% on Camelyon17 vs 84.40% for a prior anti-causal method and up to 6.7x faster transport than ODE solvers.

lessons.approach: Combining EMA weight averaging with BatchNorm in the regression setting
lessons.error_summary: EMA plus BatchNorm collapsed regression performance by 50.5 points, while buffer-free normalizations stayed stable.
lessons.applies_when: Invariant representation learning with EMA targets on regression benchmarks (Ball Agent)

lessons.approach: Naive joint optimization of task loss and strong invariance regularizers (lambda x10)
lessons.error_summary: Under high regularizer pressure, accuracy fell from 99.20% to 99.08%; projecting conflicting regularizer gradients away from the task gradient (engaged 58.8% of the time) kept 99.12%.
lessons.applies_when: Rotated MNIST with heavy invariance penalties

lessons.approach: Multi-step ODE integration (Euler, RK4) for counterfactual transport during training
lessons.error_summary: Euler (5-20 steps) and RK4 (10 steps) cost 2.9-12.5 ms/step vs 1.88 ms for one-step flow matching, with no accuracy gain (all 96.12-96.25%).
lessons.applies_when: Counterfactual latent transport in representation learning, RMNIST

lessons.question: Do you need a multi-step ODE solver for counterfactual latent transport?
lessons.answer: A one-step jump along a straight-line flow-matching velocity field is enough when paths are trained as linear optimal-transport interpolations. It matched multi-step Euler/RK4 accuracy and intervention robustness while being 1.57-6.67x faster; random-feature HSIC matched exact MMD at 4.8x lower memory.

title: CSX-MoE: Constraint-State Aware Cross-Expert Attention Fusion for Multi-Task Vehicle Routing
summary: Proposes CSX-MoE, a zero-initialized cross-expert attention layer over LoRA constraint experts in the encoder of a multi-task VRP solver, reporting better solutions than the MoSES baseline in 56 of 64 cells with under 1.5% latency overhead.

lessons.approach: Random (Kaiming) initialization of a new fusion layer's output projection when fine-tuning a pretrained routing policy
lessons.error_summary: Kaiming init caused step-0 policy degradation that fine-tuning could not recover (gap +0.1887% vs -0.0008% with zero-init).
lessons.applies_when: Adding modules to a pretrained policy and fine-tuning with REINFORCE, 16 VRP variants at N=50

lessons.approach: Unfreezing pretrained gates, residual LoRA, or the whole network while training the new fusion layer
lessons.error_summary: Unfreezing gates (+0.0273%), residual LoRA (+0.0894%) or everything (+0.3001%) worsened the gap vs the baseline, consistent with catastrophic forgetting.
lessons.applies_when: Policy-gradient fine-tuning of modular multi-task solvers

lessons.approach: Conditioning expert fusion on dynamic step-wise urgency vectors (remaining capacity, time) instead of static constraint flags
lessons.error_summary: Dynamic urgency gave no meaningful gain over static flags (1.625% vs 1.626% at N=50) while adding step-wise overhead and rollout variance; even unconditioned attention captured about 63% of the gain.
lessons.applies_when: Constraint-aware conditioning in neural VRP solvers

lessons.approach: Training without the 8x dihedral augmentation that is used at test time
lessons.error_summary: Training with 1x augmentation failed to improve the 8x-augmented test metric (+0.000% gap), while aligned 8x training gave -0.020% (15/16 variants won).
lessons.applies_when: Neural routing solvers evaluated with multi-start augmented greedy search

lessons.question: How to add a new module to a pretrained RL policy without degrading it?
lessons.answer: Zero-initialize the new module's output projection so the policy starts identical to the pretrained one, and freeze the pretrained parts. With cross-expert attention in the encoder this beat the baseline in 56/64 cells (p < 0.0001); a parameter-matched control attributed about 65% of the gain to expert interaction rather than capacity.

title: Overdamped Concentration Flow for Sample-Efficient and Rank-Preserving Vision Transformer Attribution
summary: Proposes a power-law sharpening read-out for ViT attribution maps that preserves pixel rank, reporting up to +25.88 pp Grid Pointing Game over vanilla DAVE and, with a single sample, beating 100-sample DAVE at a 93x speedup.

lessons.approach: Using very large sharpening exponents (p > 1000) for attribution maps
lessons.error_summary: Extreme exponents trigger floating-point underflow; the paper recommends p around 3.
lessons.applies_when: Power-law contrast sharpening of saliency maps

lessons.approach: Expecting monotone sharpening to improve rank-based faithfulness metrics
lessons.error_summary: Sharpening leaves pixel order unchanged (Spearman 1.0), so deletion AUC (0.7338), top-20% IoU and pixel mAP stay exactly constant; only mass-based pointing-game metrics improve.
lessons.applies_when: Evaluating attribution post-processing on ImageNet ViTs

lessons.question: How to get sharper, cheaper attribution maps for Vision Transformers?
lessons.answer: Apply a monotone power-law contrast map to the attribution instead of heavy Monte Carlo neighbourhood averaging. It suppressed background mass while keeping pixel ranks, giving +22.8/+25.9/+20.7 pp GridPG on ViT-B/DeiT-B/DeiT-III, and one sample (6.8 ms) beat 100-sample DAVE (629.8 ms).

title: Thermodynamically Stabilized Online Conformal Prediction: A Nosé–Hoover Approach to Bounded, Asymmetric Prediction Intervals
summary: Proposes FVTG-CP, a parameter-free online conformal method using a thermostat-style friction controller, tempered exponential memory and separate upper/lower channels, reporting 0.95 coverage on all twelve benchmarks with up to 28% narrower intervals and no exploding sets.

lessons.approach: Multiplicative wealth / coin-betting (universal-portfolio) updates for online conformal interval width
lessons.error_summary: Bursts of consecutive miscoverages compound the multiplicative process, producing vacuously wide intervals with peaks over 1e5x the calibrated width; alternative control rules in the ablation reached peak widths up to 2.1e6 vs 35.2 for the thermostat.
lessons.applies_when: Online conformal prediction on non-stationary financial and energy streams

lessons.approach: Uniform 1/t historical averaging of the coverage signal (the betting-method default)
lessons.error_summary: Uniform memory lagged badly after shifts: longest error run 54 vs 9, local-coverage volatility 0.106 vs 0.020, average width 382, compared with tempered exponential memory.
lessons.applies_when: Online calibration after distribution shift (AXP equity stream)

lessons.approach: Removing the volatility scale factor, or fully decoupling upper and lower scale estimators on near-symmetric data
lessons.error_summary: Without a scale, coverage dropped to 0.944 with a 0.014 gap between volatility regimes; full directional decoupling on near-symmetric equities inflated width (AMZN 135.2 vs 65.9), recovered to 76.9 by a geometric blend.
lessons.applies_when: Heteroscedastic online conformal prediction

lessons.approach: Asymmetric dual-channel interval radii without friction damping on each channel
lessons.error_summary: Disabling the thermostat friction on the two asymmetric channels let the undamped momenta diverge, giving widths around 1e5; the extra degrees of freedom need the damping.
lessons.applies_when: Online conformal prediction with separate upper/lower calibration (AXP equity stream)

lessons.question: How to keep online conformal prediction intervals from exploding after miscoverage bursts?
lessons.answer: Add a self-tuning friction (thermostat) term that damps the calibration update when miscoverage energy exceeds its target, with exponential rather than uniform memory. A single fixed configuration hit 0.95 coverage on twelve benchmarks up to 69,680 steps, cut width by up to 28%, and never produced infinite sets.

lessons.question: How to make prediction intervals narrower when residuals are skewed?
lessons.answer: Calibrate the lower and upper radii with independent controllers at alpha/2 each instead of one symmetric radius, and keep damping on both. At matched coverage (0.954 vs 0.951) the dual-channel version cut average width on AXP from 16.4 to 11.8 (-28%) and the 95% width from 42.3 to 24.4.

title: Simplified DWGR-SVL: Streamlined Spike-Driven Vision-Language Pretraining for 3D Open-World Understanding
summary: Reports that stripping wavelet, timing-lookup and curvature-gating modules from a spike-driven 3D vision-language model, keeping a Student-t kernel MMD loss, part-patch alignment and add-only geodesic propagation, reaches 83.75% zero-shot top-1 on ModelNet40 and 41.47% on Objaverse-LVIS.

lessons.approach: Re-adding complex modules (dyadic lifting wavelets, phase-resonant timing attention, curvature-gated anisotropic wave propagation) to a spike-driven 3D pretraining baseline
lessons.error_summary: Each reintroduced module lowered ModelNet40 accuracy while adding cost: wavelets +4.19M params and -0.40%; phase-resonant attention +3.15M dense float MACs and -0.77%; curvature gating (over 1M 3x3 eigen-decompositions) -4.01%.
lessons.applies_when: Spiking point-cloud encoders aligned to CLIP, 3,000-shape controlled probe, T=4

lessons.approach: Learnable Student-t degrees of freedom in the kernel MMD alignment loss
lessons.error_summary: A learnable nu converged to 1.709 and reached 61.83% ModelNet40 accuracy versus 63.78% with a fixed small nu=0.5.
lessons.applies_when: Distribution alignment between spike firing rates and continuous CLIP embeddings

lessons.approach: Multi-hop geodesic propagation (H>=2) over point-center graphs
lessons.error_summary: Two or more hops over-smoothed features; a single hop was best (55.75%, +0.97 over standard k-NN).
lessons.applies_when: Graph aggregation in spike-driven point-cloud encoders, ablation scale

lessons.question: How do I improve zero-shot accuracy of a spiking 3D vision-language model without breaking spike-driven efficiency?
lessons.answer: Prefer a few simple, add-only components over elaborate float-heavy modules. The paper keeps a heavy-tailed Student-t kernel MMD loss, single-scale part-patch alignment (16 parts) and one-hop add-only geodesic propagation, reporting 83.75% ModelNet40 / 41.47% Objaverse-LVIS zero-shot (+1.65 / +1.37 over the spike baseline) at 7.23 mJ per sample, about 45x below a large ANN foundation model.

title: Time-Varying Complex Spectral Modulation Implicit Forecaster for Non-Stationary Time Series Forecasting
summary: Proposes adding zero-initialized, tanh-bounded time-varying amplitude gain and phase drift fields over raised-cosine temporal frames to a static Fourier (iDFT) forecasting decoder, reporting a 2.15% average test MSE reduction over 14 benchmarks and up to 20.34% on PEMS04.

lessons.approach: Modulating the full spectrum (all 360 frequency bins) instead of only the lowest 128
lessons.error_summary: Full-spectrum modulation gave no accuracy gain (ETTh1 MSE 0.496 vs 0.495) while adding 38% parameters and 40% training time (PEMS04 877s to 1451s per epoch).
lessons.applies_when: Spectral decoders for long-horizon multivariate forecasting

lessons.approach: Time-invariant or too-fine temporal frames for the modulation fields (raised-cosine window count W)
lessons.error_summary: PEMS04 MSE followed an inverted U: W=1 0.283, W=2 0.234, W=4 0.192, W=8 0.205, W=16 0.218. Too few windows cannot track bursts; too many inject high-frequency noise.
lessons.applies_when: Time-varying Fourier decoders on non-stationary traffic data, long horizons 96-720

lessons.approach: Unbounded modulation heads or Xavier initialization instead of zero-init plus tanh bounds
lessons.error_summary: Unbounded projections amplified long-horizon phase drift and Xavier init injected random spectral distortion at step 0; zero-init with tanh bounds gave the lowest error (ETTh1 0.495, PEMS04 0.192).
lessons.applies_when: Residual modulation on top of a pretrained-style static spectral prior

lessons.approach: Applying time-varying spectral modulation to stationary or noisy series
lessons.error_summary: On Exchange, Solar and ETTm1 the static Fourier prior was already optimal; the method only falls back to it (no gain) rather than helping.
lessons.applies_when: Datasets with strong stationarity or high white-noise ratio

lessons.question: How can a frequency-domain forecaster handle non-stationary bursts and phase lag over long horizons?
lessons.answer: Let a static Fourier decoder learn bounded, smooth time-varying amplitude and phase corrections that start at zero. Gains and phase drifts parameterized over 4 raised-cosine frames on the 128 lowest bins, zero-initialized and tanh-bounded, cut mean MSE 0.423 to 0.411 across 14 benchmarks and PEMS04 MSE 0.114 to 0.091; phase drift alone gave +4.87% on PEMS04, both together +20.34%.

title: Riemannian Momentum-Transported Spectral Optimization for Language Model Pretraining
summary: Proposes a spectral-sphere optimizer that parallel-transports momentum to the current tangent space, adds a stable-rank isotropization term and solves the dual with a 2D Krylov system, reporting a 2.0x wall-clock speedup over the Spectral Sphere Optimizer (7,212s vs 14,404s) with lower validation loss (3.3297 vs 3.3452) on a 153M model.

lessons.approach: Ad-hoc retracted renormalization of momentum on the spectral sphere instead of tangent-space transport
lessons.error_summary: Orthogonal momentum leakage reached 0.1692 (vs 0.0017 for parallel transport, 0.0041 Euclidean) and loss diverged (4.19 vs 3.76).
lessons.applies_when: Norm-constrained spectral optimizers for transformer pretraining, 153M params

lessons.approach: Isotropization step taken with the literal ascent sign on the stable-rank gradient
lessons.error_summary: The ascent sign accelerated rank collapse (stable rank 171.2 to 141.2); the corrected descent sign raised it to 183.7.
lessons.applies_when: Rank-preserving regularizers inside spectral optimizers

lessons.approach: Larger Krylov subspace (k=4 or 8) for the dual Lagrange solve
lessons.error_summary: Converged residual barely improved (0.394 to 0.360) while latency rose from 3.00 to 7.36 ms per call; final loss was flat across solver settings.
lessons.applies_when: Dual root-finding in spectral-sphere optimizers

lessons.approach: Aggressive matrix preconditioners (SOAP, Sophia-G) and AdamW as LLM pretraining baselines
lessons.error_summary: SOAP reached lower training loss (3.2852) but 0.36 points lower downstream accuracy; Sophia-G had the worst rank collapse (stable rank 27.9); AdamW stable rank fell 38.5 to 3.5 from layer 1 to 12 with vanishing pre-activation gradients.
lessons.applies_when: 153M Qwen3-style transformer on FineWeb-Edu, 492M tokens

lessons.question: How do I keep a spectral-norm-constrained optimizer fast and avoid rank collapse in deep layers?
lessons.answer: Keep momentum in the tangent plane and solve the dual in a tiny subspace rather than with full-tensor bisection. Projecting momentum onto the current tangent space, adding a stable-rank isotropization force and a 2x2 Krylov dual solve (6.1x faster per call: 3.00 vs 18.38 ms) gave 2.0x end-to-end speedup over SSO and 38.81% vs 38.48% zero-shot accuracy, with stable rank staying near 87 at 3.06B tokens while AdamW's decayed.

title: Graph Poisson Optimal Transport Decoding: Single-Pass Geometry-Aware Truncation for LLMs
summary: Proposes a training-free decoding rule that replaces iterative Wasserstein Top-W refinement with one regularized graph Poisson solve over 200 candidate tokens plus a Dirichlet-energy adaptive mass rule, reporting flat accuracy across temperatures (77.2% GSM8K on LLaMA-3.1-8B at T=2.0 vs Top-p's 2.65%) and a 3.42x speedup over Top-W.

lessons.approach: Top-p and Min-p truncation at high sampling temperature
lessons.error_summary: Top-p collapsed to 2.65% flexible GSM8K accuracy on LLaMA-3.1-8B at T=2.0 (0.5%/0.0% in another setting) and Min-p degraded sharply as temperature rose.
lessons.applies_when: Stochastic decoding for math/science reasoning, T>=1.0, 3B-8B models

lessons.approach: Single-pass distance-to-set potential (Top-W without alternating refinement)
lessons.error_summary: It was bit-identical to a zero potential: it only penalized low-probability tokens already removed by mass cropping, so it became a no-op.
lessons.applies_when: Geometry-aware truncation samplers

lessons.approach: Static mass parameter in geometry-aware truncation
lessons.error_summary: Static mass lost 3.0 points of GSM8K accuracy at T=2.0 versus Dirichlet-energy adaptive mass (83.5 vs 86.5 on Phi-3-Mini).
lessons.applies_when: High-temperature decoding with OT-style truncation

lessons.approach: Fixed kernel bandwidth (sigma^2=0.1) for the candidate-token graph
lessons.error_summary: The graph disconnected (algebraic connectivity about 0.009) whereas dynamic median bandwidth kept it connected (about 120).
lessons.applies_when: Building similarity graphs over token embeddings at each decoding step

lessons.question: How do I keep LLM reasoning accuracy stable when sampling at high temperature?
lessons.answer: Adapt the retained probability mass to the step's uncertainty instead of using a fixed nucleus threshold. The paper found the adaptive mass rule is the main stabilizer: distilled alone into a scalar sampler (beta-Top-p) it stays flat across T in [0.5, 2.0] at Top-p latency, while the graph Poisson potential (0.679 ms/token solve) acts only as a tie-breaker.

lessons.question: How can geometry-aware OT decoding be made cheap enough for serving?
lessons.answer: Replace multi-pass alternating OT refinement with one closed-form linear solve on a small candidate graph. A 200x200 regularized graph Poisson system (gamma=0.01, cosine distance, accuracy saturating at 200 candidates) solved in under 0.7 ms gave 3.42x isolated and up to 16.71x loaded speedup over iterative Top-W.

title: Balanced-Flow Deep Flow Networks: Zero-Sum Matrix Parameterization and Dual-Prioritized Search for Discrete Optimization Surrogates
summary: Proposes enforcing boundary mass balance in Deep Flow Network surrogates via a soft zero-sum matrix parameterization and ranking local-search swaps by dual node potentials, reporting up to 2.17x lower test MSE (1.322e-3 vs 2.873e-3 on Quadratic) and 22x-79x fewer solver evaluations in downstream search.

lessons.approach: Unconstrained boundary-matrix parameterization in Deep Flow Networks (lambda=0) with high-cost fallback arcs
lessons.error_summary: Net-outflow imbalance dumped demand onto fallback arcs; dual potentials scaled with the penalty cost and accuracy degraded as the penalty grew, corrupting straight-through subgradients and raising training variance.
lessons.applies_when: Neural surrogates of discrete convex functions (Convex Quadratic, Resource Allocation)

lessons.approach: Enforcing mass balance on a flow-native problem (MDVSP vehicle scheduling)
lessons.error_summary: On MDVSP the unconstrained model (lambda=0) performed best, so a single global balance strength does not fit all datasets; the paper needed a per-dataset or automatically selected lambda.
lessons.applies_when: Surrogate problems whose natural structure is already a flow

lessons.approach: Prediction-guided M-convex steepest descent as the downstream search on the learned surrogate
lessons.error_summary: It needed 46.4x-69.1x more min-cost-flow solves (cold) and 15.0x-20.5x more (warm-started) than dual-prioritized search at matched quality; Quad wall-clock 30.0s vs 1.46s.
lessons.applies_when: Local search over integer points on a learned flow surrogate

lessons.question: How do I make a learned min-cost-flow surrogate train stably and search fast?
lessons.answer: Build exact mass balance into the parameterization and rank local-search moves by dual node potentials. A zero-sum column-differencing matrix applied after rounding removed demand-dumping and STE variance spikes, and dual-prioritized descent cut solver evaluations 22x-79x; an imbalance-triggered controller picked lambda>0 for convex tasks and lambda=0 for MDVSP, matching hand tuning.

title: Null-Space Kernel Vector-Balanced Active Inference for Prediction-Powered Estimation
summary: Proposes balancing active-sampling designs on RKHS kernel eigenvectors projected orthogonal to the model predictions, so balancing cannot cancel the control variate, reporting 9.1% average (up to 14.4%) narrower 90% confidence intervals than cube-active sampling and up to 77% label-budget savings with nominal coverage.

lessons.approach: Naive feature balancing (unprojected kernel PCA, raw feature PCA, direct prediction balancing) in prediction-powered active inference
lessons.error_summary: Unprojected directions were strongly collinear with the predictions (0.76-0.97), risking algebraic cancellation of the control variate, and gave less steady coverage (worst case at most 0.882 vs 0.894).
lessons.applies_when: Active sampling with a balanced (Cube) design and ML predictions as a control variate

lessons.approach: Using many null-space eigenvectors (K=50) as balancing constraints
lessons.error_summary: CI narrowed more (+7.2% vs +3.0% at K=15) but coverage slipped to 0.869-0.878 below nominal 0.90 and runtime grew 12x (16.6 to 197.9 ms per trial).
lessons.applies_when: Cube balanced sampling, budget 0.10

lessons.approach: Tight-frame (inverse square-root Fisher) and outer-product score balancing for vector M-estimation
lessons.error_summary: These variants under-covered (0.846-0.862) whereas raw score-vector balancing stayed valid and beat scalar balancing by 22.9% on Linear.
lessons.applies_when: Multi-parameter M-estimation under label budgets

lessons.question: How do I use feature balancing in active prediction-powered inference without breaking the control variate?
lessons.answer: Balance only on feature directions orthogonal to the prediction vector. Projecting the kernel matrix off the prediction space and keeping about min(15, N/150) leading null-space eigenvectors, with a conformalized quantile regression uncertainty target, narrowed 90% CIs by 9.1% on average over 11 datasets while keeping coverage near nominal; gains held across RBF, Laplacian, polynomial and linear kernels (about +12%).

title: Flash-Newton: Fused IO-Aware Dual Newton-CG for Fast Convergence in Ultra-Small Regularization Entropic Optimal Transport
summary: Proposes a matrix-free Schur-complement dual Newton-CG solver for entropic optimal transport with streaming Triton kernels, a Schur-Jacobi preconditioner and geometric epsilon-scaling, reporting 1.4x-68.1x speedups over FlashSinkhorn at O((n+m)d) memory for epsilon <= 0.005.

lessons.approach: Classical dual Newton for entropic OT that materializes the transport plan or full dual Hessian
lessons.error_summary: At n,m >= 20,000 it runs out of memory: the plan would need 1.49 GB and the Hessian 5.96 GB, versus at most 20 MB for the matrix-free formulations.
lessons.applies_when: Large point clouds, entropic OT with second-order solvers

lessons.approach: Cold-start Newton or a linear epsilon ladder without geometric epsilon-scaling
lessons.error_summary: Cold-start Newton diverged (NaN marginal error) and the linear ladder failed to enter the quadratic basin (residual 1.03); geometric scaling entered it in 271 ms and reached 1e-3 in 3.4 s.
lessons.applies_when: Ultra-small entropic regularization, epsilon <= 0.01

lessons.approach: Undamped or over-damped Tikhonov ridge in the Newton-CG Schur system
lessons.error_summary: tau=0 left the Schur complement singular and did not converge (CG stalls at relative residual 6.5e4 without the ridge); tau=1e-2 over-damped toward gradient descent; tau=1e-4 worked.
lessons.applies_when: Dual Hessians with a translation null space

lessons.approach: Adaptive early-exit rules for switching from Sinkhorn to Newton
lessons.error_summary: Rules based on dual rate or gradient thresholds succeeded on only 4/7 or 5/7 datasets, switching too early on ill-conditioned cases and stalling; a fixed two-level schedule succeeded 7/7 and was fastest on 6/7.
lessons.applies_when: Hybrid first/second-order OT solvers across 7 datasets, d from 16 to 512

lessons.question: How do I get high-precision entropic OT plans at tiny epsilon without running out of GPU memory?
lessons.answer: Run dual Newton-CG matrix-free on a reduced Schur system and warm it into the quadratic basin with geometric epsilon-scaling. Streaming Hessian-vector products, a Schur-Jacobi diagonal preconditioner, inexact CG tolerance min(0.1, sqrt of gradient norm) (77% fewer CG steps than a 1e-8 tolerance) and damping 1e-4 gave 1.4x-68.1x speedups over FlashSinkhorn in strict fp32.

title: Global Ensemble-Coupled Tree-Spline Hoeffding Decomposition for Tree Ensembles
summary: Proposes a post-hoc explanation of tree ensembles that fits continuous linear B-splines anchored at split thresholds in one globally coupled solve with Laplacian smoothing, then projects for hierarchical orthogonality, reporting 0.0%-0.5% residual error, max |corr| <= 0.003 and 3-8x lower local attribution variability than TreeSHAP on 9 UCI datasets.

lessons.approach: Solving the functional decomposition per tree (or in small groups) instead of one global ensemble solve
lessons.error_summary: Per-tree fits accumulated cross-tree boundary misalignments: residual MSE rose 129x on Abalone (0.02% to 2.93%), 4x on Airfoil (0.47% to 1.79%), and Housing 0.00% to 1.79%.
lessons.applies_when: Hoeffding decomposition explanations of tree ensembles

lessons.approach: Placing spline knots at data quantiles instead of split thresholds, or using higher-order (C1, C2) splines
lessons.error_summary: Quantile knots raised residual MSE by 18% (analytical) and 23% on Bike Sharing; higher-order splines tripled runtime on Superconductivity (908s to 2694s) without lowering error.
lessons.applies_when: Spline-based decompositions of piecewise-constant tree models

lessons.approach: Plain L2 ridge regularization to fill empty grid regions
lessons.error_summary: In an artificial empty-cell hole, ridge gave in-hole MSE 0.2744 vs 0.1671 for adjacent-knot Laplacian smoothing (unregularized 0.3827): ridge shrinks coefficients but does not smooth across gaps.
lessons.applies_when: Sparse or low-density regions of the feature grid

lessons.approach: TreeSHAP for separating main effects and interactions under correlated features
lessons.error_summary: TreeSHAP failed to isolate interactions under correlation (max |corr| 0.392 vs 0.047) and showed higher local attribution noise.
lessons.applies_when: Tree ensembles on dependent inputs

lessons.question: How do I get smooth, exactly reconstructing, orthogonal main-effect and interaction explanations from a tree ensemble?
lessons.answer: Fit continuous linear splines anchored at the ensemble's split thresholds in one global solve, then enforce orthogonality by projection in coefficient space. This reported near-zero residual error (0.0%-0.5%) and max |corr| <= 0.003 (<= 0.125 out of sample); interaction order 2 dropped Housing residual 11.2% to 0.0%, and order 3 recovered a true 3-way term with 14.5x lower MSE.

title: Cellular Sheaf-Gated Multi-Scale Partial Tree-Sliced Wasserstein
summary: Proposes using k-NN cellular sheaf coboundary residuals as per-point consistency scores that both reroute outliers in a tree-sliced Wasserstein splitting map and gate transported mass, reporting 0.00% outlier capture with lowest Chamfer distance (0.00182) on noisy point-cloud registration and full accuracy-fidelity control on class-imbalanced face translation.

lessons.approach: Balanced sliced OT (SW, Db-TSW) and unbalanced baselines (SUOT, SPOT) on outlier-contaminated measures
lessons.error_summary: Balanced metrics refit the outlier mode (noise capture 15.08% and 15.96%); unbalanced SUOT (66.34%) and SPOT (20.26%) also failed to isolate outliers; entropic solvers ran 50-90x slower.
lessons.applies_when: Point-cloud alignment and generative modeling with spatial outliers

lessons.approach: Non-robust min-max rescaling (or two-sided soft exponential) to calibrate per-point consistency gates
lessons.error_summary: A single extreme residual corrupted the global min-max scale (Chamfer 0.00311 vs 0.00182 for median+MAD; MNIST outlier rate up to 4.56%); two-sided exponential attenuated valid inliers (0.00363).
lessons.applies_when: Turning local residuals into outlier-gating weights

lessons.approach: Random k-regular graph instead of a spatial k-NN graph for the sheaf
lessons.error_summary: Gate discrimination collapsed from 1624x to 3.2x and the outlier rate rose to 0.92%.
lessons.applies_when: Graph-based local consistency scores

lessons.approach: Local mass gating alone without a global target-mass factor on class-imbalanced data
lessons.error_summary: Fixed one operating point (accuracy 85.95%, LPIPS 0.4063); composing with a global mass factor swept accuracy 81.72%-99.59%.
lessons.applies_when: Class-imbalanced image-to-image translation with partial OT

lessons.question: How do I make sliced optimal transport robust to outliers without hand-tuning target mass?
lessons.answer: Score each point by local geometric consistency on a spatial k-NN graph with robust (median+MAD) calibration and use it to gate transported mass. Mass gating alone took noise capture from 84% inliers to 100% (0.00% outliers), and caching the gate with chunked GPU k-NN cut peak memory 84.8x (32.9 vs 2791.5 MB) at baseline runtime.

title: Legendrian Contact-Geometric Discount Optimization with Dimension-Adaptive Dirichlet Regularization for High-Dimensional Quality-Diversity
summary: Proposes a finite-difference Dirichlet smoothness penalty on the neural discount model of Discount Model Search, scaled by c(k)=c0*max(0,1-2/k) so it is off in 2D, reporting +422 QD score on 10D LP Sphere and +217 on 10D Rastrigin (p<0.01) with parity at k>=20.

lessons.approach: Unregularized MLP discount surrogate in Discount Model Search at measure dimension k>=10
lessons.error_summary: Sparse emitter sampling let the MLP learn spurious high-frequency wiggles in unvisited gaps, miscalibrating improvement rankings and stalling frontier expansion (10D Sphere QD 6,431 vs 6,853 with the penalty).
lessons.applies_when: Continuous surrogate-assisted quality-diversity, 10D+ measure spaces

lessons.approach: Spectral normalization or L1 total variation as the smoothness regularizer for the discount model
lessons.error_summary: Spectral norm collapsed on rugged 10D Rastrigin (4,980 QD, below unregularized 5,129 and L2 Dirichlet 5,346); L1 TV made flat plateaus and cut 10D Rastrigin coverage to 83.28% vs 87.42%.
lessons.applies_when: Multi-basin quality-diversity landscapes

lessons.approach: Exact autograd gradient penalty (with or without Gaussian input noise) instead of finite-difference directional probes
lessons.error_summary: Autograd L2 scored lower (6,590 vs 6,853 on 10D Sphere); adding input noise recovered only 9% of the gap.
lessons.applies_when: Smoothness penalties on neural surrogates

lessons.approach: Expecting the regularizer to help in very high-dimensional measure spaces (20D-784D)
lessons.error_summary: Statistically significant gains appeared only at k=10; at k>=20 the method only matched DMS (parity, no regression).
lessons.applies_when: Quality-diversity with 20D to 784D measure spaces

lessons.question: How do I stop a neural surrogate from oscillating in unvisited regions of a high-dimensional search space?
lessons.answer: Add a finite-difference L2 Dirichlet smoothness penalty whose weight grows with dimension and vanishes in low dimensions. A coefficient c(k)=c0*max(0,1-2/k) with c0=0.00625, 16 random directions (16x lower gradient variance at about 15-20 ms/step) and step 0.05 matched DMS in 2D and gave significant gains at 10D with zero non-finite losses.

title: DosePFN: Amortized In-Context Continuous Dose-Response and Marginal Causal Effect Estimation
summary: Proposes a prior-fitted transformer with a continuous-treatment prior, a scale-invariant quantile head, Fourier dose encodings and a monotone quadrature layer, plus a kurtosis-and-overlap router between quantile and histogram heads, reporting 0.00% monotonicity violations and parity with CausalPFN on light-tailed binary suites while improving heavy-tailed LalondePSID.

lessons.approach: Routing between quantile and histogram heads on a single signal (kurtosis only, overlap only, or factual fit)
lessons.error_summary: Kurtosis-only wrongly routed heavy-tailed but well-overlapped ACIC (PEHE 0.73 to 0.85); overlap-only misrouted LalondeCPS (8.81 to 9.00 x1e3); factual fit decoupled from causal accuracy and was right on only 2/4 suites; no static blend weight dominated.
lessons.applies_when: Choosing decoder heads for amortized causal effect estimation

lessons.approach: Quantile decoder without context affine normalization
lessons.error_summary: Removing normalization inflated LalondePSID PEHE from 14.46e3 to 22.59e3 and continuous NRMSE 0.211 to 0.317.
lessons.applies_when: Heavy-tailed, wide-range outcomes in PFN causal models

lessons.approach: L1, L2 or histogram losses instead of pinball loss for the quantile head
lessons.error_summary: Heavy-tailed PEHE was worse (L1 14.69e3, L2 15.48e3, histogram 15.71e3 vs pinball 14.46e3).
lessons.applies_when: Heavy-tailed outcome regression

lessons.question: How do I add continuous or heavy-tailed outcome support to an amortized causal model without hurting light-tailed accuracy?
lessons.answer: Gate the new head with a conjunction of observable data statistics rather than replacing the old one. Using the quantile head only when outcome excess kurtosis > 1.0 and propensity ROC-AUC > 0.8 matched the per-suite oracle on 4/4 suites, and on 20 unseen datasets the cutoff sat on a 0%-misroute plateau with PEHE regret 3.5%-4.6%.

title: DisCoRe-IQA: Disentangled Content-Quality Representation and Region-Level Segmentation for Lightweight Image Quality Assessment
summary: Proposes a lightweight IQA model with LoRA adaptation, adversarial content removal via a gradient reversal layer against semantic clusters, and a region-level defect segmentation head, reporting content-probe accuracy dropping from 0.868 to 0.138 and an 89.6% worst-region localization hit-rate with under 1.0M trainable parameters.

lessons.approach: Unsupervised PCA-nulling to remove content bias from quality embeddings
lessons.error_summary: It barely removed content (probe accuracy 0.807 vs 0.868 raw) and degraded out-of-domain scoring (PLCC 0.7219).
lessons.applies_when: Content-quality disentanglement in vision-language IQA features

lessons.approach: Soft independence penalties (HSIC, MINE) for content removal
lessons.error_summary: They cut content probe accuracy (0.018 / 0.082) but also suppressed quality features, dropping OOD PLCC below the raw baseline (0.7743 / 0.7734 vs 0.7755).
lessons.applies_when: Removing a nuisance factor that correlates with the target

lessons.approach: Training a patch defect head with only global MOS multiple-instance supervision
lessons.error_summary: It failed on localized defects (correlation 0.182, 46.4% hit-rate) versus 0.530 and 89.6% when joint synthetic local defects were added.
lessons.applies_when: Weakly supervised localization of image quality defects

lessons.question: How do I remove content bias from an image quality representation without destroying quality signal?
lessons.answer: Use a supervised adversary against explicit semantic clusters via a gradient reversal layer rather than unsupervised nulling or independence penalties. Content probe accuracy fell to 0.138 while OOD PLCC rose to 0.7934, and low-level quality signals kept 79%-110% of their strength (in-domain MOS SRCC 0.900 to 0.917).

lessons.question: How can a small IQA model localize defects as well as a grounding MLLM?
lessons.answer: Train a patch-level head on synthetic localized defects with continuous overlap targets, anchored to real MOS through MIL. It matched a grounding MLLM hit-rate (89.6% vs 89.3%) at about 2,949x lower latency (0.56 vs 1,638 ms) and kept 92% of its hit-rate on non-rectangular defect shapes.

title: Cellular Sheaf Laplacian and Spectral Koopman-Invariant Temporal Sparse Autoencoders
summary: Proposes a temporal sparse autoencoder with a boundary-gated sheaf Laplacian, a spectrally bounded intra-sequence Koopman operator, straight-through support-preserved projection and cohomology-based capacity allocation, reporting wins on 12/12 semantics and context probing benchmarks on Pythia-160m and Gemma-2-2b at FVE about 0.904 and 0.690.

lessons.approach: Continuous (non-support-masked) alignment gradients in a temporal SAE
lessons.error_summary: Liveness was 11% lower (fraction alive 0.748 vs 0.853 with straight-through support projection) and context accuracy fell (0.819 vs 0.861) from over-smoothing.
lessons.applies_when: Temporal/sequence-level SAEs on LLM residual streams

lessons.approach: Unconstrained dense Koopman operator for feature dynamics
lessons.error_summary: The operator norm grew to 4.965 (Pythia) and 2.267 (Gemma), i.e. expansive dynamics; it fit short horizons better, but spectral bounding to norm <= 1 was needed for non-expansiveness.
lessons.applies_when: Linear latent dynamics models in interpretability

lessons.approach: Dynamic capacity allocation via sheaf cohomology rank (dim H0) during training
lessons.error_summary: The coboundary soft-SVD dominated the forward pass (65.9%/86.8% of time); replacing it with static partitioning gave a 5.3x speedup, bringing overhead over Temporal SAE to +55% on Gemma and +101% on Pythia.
lessons.applies_when: Adaptive dictionary capacity in SAEs

lessons.approach: Contrastive InfoNCE term in temporal SAE training
lessons.error_summary: It costs reconstruction: omitting it raised FVE (0.919 vs 0.897) but hurt context probing; InfoNCE alone degraded as steeply as Temporal SAE on liveness.
lessons.applies_when: Reconstruction vs semantic probing trade-off in SAEs

lessons.question: How do I make sparse autoencoders capture long-range semantic features rather than local syntax?
lessons.answer: Add intra-sequence temporal structure (boundary-gated smoothness and a norm-bounded forward dynamics operator) and confine alignment gradients to active features. This won 12/12 probing cells and improved SAEBench top-1 sparse probing (0.7802 vs 0.7591 on Pythia) while keeping reconstruction; learned Koopman operators beat identity persistence at every horizon (k=5 MSE 0.973 vs 1.270).

title: Neural Tangent Woodbury Exact Auctions with Inequality-Averse Social Welfare
summary: Proposes an accuracy auction that maps bids through Kolm-Pollak inequality-averse utility with ex-ante budget caps, trains in an NTK space with a localized RBF defense kernel, and prices exactly with a rank-1 Woodbury path solver, reporting a 17.2x payment speedup, discrepancy below 7.28e-15 and lower strategic gaming flip rates (0.377 vs 0.501).

lessons.approach: Linear bid weighting (weight = bid) in accuracy auctions
lessons.error_summary: Weights reached 11.87x on high earners, distorting the boundary and dropping accuracy to 0.4917; Kolm-Pollak capped weights at 2.40x (allocation Gini 0.3650 vs 0.4884).
lessons.applies_when: Income-linked bids on ACSIncome

lessons.approach: Post-hoc payment truncation to enforce budgets
lessons.error_summary: Truncation removed individual-rationality violations (unconstrained had 0.73%) but broke allocation monotonicity, producing 4.65% DSIC violations among budget-constrained agents.
lessons.applies_when: Auctions with 30% budget-constrained agents

lessons.approach: Linear feature-manipulation penalty as a defense against strategic gaming
lessons.error_summary: The penalty collapsed to an affine shift (fit R2 = 1.0000) and its flip rate (0.508) gave no protection over the undefended NTK (0.501).
lessons.applies_when: Gradient-based feature manipulation by negative agents

lessons.question: How do I compute exact truthful payments in an accuracy auction with a nonlinear model?
lessons.answer: Use a stable kernel model whose prediction is a closed-form function of one agent's weight, so the critical bid is found in one scalar step. A rank-1 Woodbury path in NTK space matched brute-force re-solves to 7.275e-15 at 17.2x speed, payments stayed O(1) in population size, and ex-ante budget caps kept 0.00% IR and 0.00% DSIC violations.

title: Task-Adaptive Functional-Affinity Tokenization and Phase-Adaptive Regional Attention for EEG Foundation Models
summary: Proposes four zero-initialized residual adapters (about 0.12M parameters) on a frozen CSBrain EEG backbone and reports a +0.0154 macro-average balanced-accuracy gain across four BCI benchmarks, with +5.9 points over LoRA when transferred to two other EEG backbones.

lessons.approach: Blend an unnormalized binary 10-20 anatomical adjacency matrix with a unit-mass functional covariance matrix for soft spatial tokenization
lessons.error_summary: Anatomical row sums equal electrode degree and dwarf the functional term by up to 12.8x; the binary branch was actively harmful (macro delta -0.0053 balanced accuracy). Degree-normalizing it turned the module net-positive (+0.0117).
lessons.applies_when: Mixing graph adjacencies of different row mass in EEG spatial tokenizers

lessons.approach: Functional-affinity spatial routing on a dense 64-channel montage (PhysioNet-MI)
lessons.error_summary: Neutral to slightly negative (delta -0.0010, within 0.0056 std) because dense adjacency is already complete; it helped sparse montages (+0.0115 BCIC-IV-2a, +0.0373 MentalArithmetic) and became positive (+0.0035) only after removing 30% of channels.
lessons.applies_when: Dense EEG montages where every region is already connected

lessons.approach: Use a high adapter learning-rate multiplier (0.50x) on a small downstream EEG dataset
lessons.error_summary: On MentalArithmetic (n=1,217) 0.50x overfit (-0.0375) while 0.25x gained +0.0331; on data-rich PhysioNet-MI (n=5,188) 0.50x was best (+0.0213). A uniform adapter learning rate is wrong for one of the two regimes.
lessons.applies_when: PEFT of EEG foundation models across datasets with under or over about 2,000 training samples

lessons.approach: Unconstrained dense global inter-window attention instead of a local neighbourhood of radius 1-2
lessons.error_summary: Dense global attention added 3.57 GB (+36.9%) peak memory without beating the local radius-1-2 neighbourhood on accuracy.
lessons.applies_when: Temporal inter-window attention in EEG transformers

lessons.question: How to adapt a frozen EEG foundation model to small downstream BCI datasets without representation drift?
lessons.answer: Use zero-initialized residual adapters, so the model starts identical to the frozen backbone, and scale the adapter learning rate by training-set size. The paper reports a +0.0154 macro balanced-accuracy gain with no significant per-dataset regression (+2.13% on PhysioNet-MI, p=0.028) using about 0.12M parameters, under 0.85% of the backbone; a size threshold near n=2,000 performed like a smooth log-sigmoid rule.

lessons.question: Which pooling should replace regional mean-pooling of EEG channels?
lessons.answer: Attentive covariance-preserving regional aggregation outperformed uniform mean-pooling for focal motor-cortex signals. In leave-one-out ablation on PhysioNet-MI it was the most load-bearing adapter (removing it cost -0.0077 balanced accuracy), followed by spectral-saliency scale routing (-0.0058).

title: KinemaAnchor-Manifold: Functional Feasibility Post-Processing for Articulated, Simulation-Ready Scene Generation
summary: Proposes a post-processing stage that binds nested objects to moving link frames and clears articulation swept volumes, reporting nested-object retention under joint motion rising from 0.7% to 97.7% and 53.6% of movable-blocker obstructions cleared (vs 0.0%) on a 210-prompt corpus.

lessons.approach: Static physical post-processing that treats articulated assets as rigid bodies in their closed rest pose and anchors contents in world coordinates
lessons.error_summary: Scenes passed collision and stability checks, yet 8.0% of articulation sweeps were obstructed and only 0.7% of 2,569 nested manipulands stayed with their drawer or shelf when the joint moved.
lessons.applies_when: Simulation-ready indoor scenes from agentic generators (about 101 objects per scene) used for manipulation

lessons.approach: Treat every object near a swept volume as a blocker to move, rather than only movable clutter
lessons.error_summary: Solver convergence dropped to 26.9% versus 46.2% with a movable-only blocker filter on 26 cabinet-cabinet conflict scenes.
lessons.applies_when: Multi-state pose optimization clearing articulation sweeps

lessons.approach: Continuous swept-volume keep-out vs a cheap two-endpoint approximation; adding semantic distortion weighting to the objective
lessons.error_summary: The two-endpoint approximation under-covers the sweep by 25% yet changed clearance by only +0.08 pp while being 2.54x cheaper; semantic weighting moved furniture under 1 cm and left feasibility identical. Both refinements bought nothing on quarter-turn doors.
lessons.applies_when: Scene libraries without wide-swing articulation

lessons.question: How to keep objects inside drawers and cabinets attached when the joint opens in a generated simulation scene?
lessons.answer: Bind nested objects to the moving link frame instead of world coordinates, and settle them with their link during gravity settling. The paper reports retention rising from 0.7% to 97.7%, and anchored seating raised static stability on affected scenes from 92.5% to 100%, with zero collisions preserved.

title: TabHarmony: In-Context Harmonic Feature Expansion and Conformal Risk-Gated Early Exit for Tabular Foundation Models
summary: Proposes a training-free inference wrapper for tabular PFNs that fills unused padding slots with polynomial feature expansions, gates features by correlation eigenmodes, and exits early under conformal risk control, reporting mean AUC 0.8944 to 0.8957 across 300 TALENT datasets and 28.7% compute savings.

lessons.approach: Always inject both polynomial expansion and spectral correlation gating into the prompt (forced combination)
lessons.error_summary: Gave +0.0072 AUC on average but caused regressions on 3 of 30 datasets from prompt over-saturation; an inner-CV guard choosing per dataset removed all regressions and reached +0.0078 AUC, +0.0203 R2.
lessons.applies_when: Training-free prompt enrichment of frozen tabular in-context models

lessons.approach: Raise per-feature polynomial expansion degree beyond 3
lessons.error_summary: Regression R2 peaked at degree 3 (0.7191) and fell at degree 4 (0.7165) as extra coordinates exhausted the fixed 100-feature padding budget.
lessons.applies_when: Backbones with a fixed maximum feature count

lessons.approach: Haar framelet subband features and untuned random Fourier features as input expansions
lessons.error_summary: Haar subbands gave near-zero change (delta AUC about -0.0001) and untuned random Fourier features showed no gain (0.8746 vs 0.8745 linear baseline AUC).
lessons.applies_when: Feature expansion for tabular PFNs

lessons.approach: Uncalibrated fixed entropy thresholds or fixed layer truncation for early exit
lessons.error_summary: Reported to degrade sharply on difficult tables and to be dominated on the accuracy-compute frontier by conformally calibrated thresholds.
lessons.applies_when: Per-query online early exit in tabular transformers

lessons.question: How to improve a frozen tabular foundation model at inference time without ever making it worse?
lessons.answer: Add enrichments only when an inner cross-validation on the support set shows they help, else fall back to the untouched prompt. Smooth per-feature expansion to degree 3 in unused padding slots (Legendre, Chebyshev and Fourier performed alike) gave gains rising to +0.0146 AUC on the datasets where it switched on, and the largest gains in low-data regimes (+0.1315 AUC at 128 support rows).

lessons.question: How to do early exit in a transformer with a risk guarantee per query?
lessons.answer: Calibrate layer-wise predictive-entropy exit thresholds on held-out support data with split conformal risk control. The paper reports realized violation at or below target for every risk budget, 96.2% agreement with full depth at 24.8% savings for a 0.05 budget, and 28.7% average depth savings in strict online deployment.

title: RES-TRACE: Residual-Stream Layer-Wise Proximity Flow for Efficient and Faithful Long-Context Attribution
summary: Proposes a single-pass attribution method that propagates a sign vector of the summed target hidden states through value projections with a positive gate and linear depth weighting, reporting evidence recovery 0.695 vs 0.635 for the best baseline on RULER and lower deletion errors in 13 of 13 settings.

lessons.approach: Weight intermediate chain-of-thought tokens by their prior relevance scores (hop-0, softmax, or top-20%) when building the recursive attribution target
lessons.error_summary: All weighted variants worsened faithfulness: MATH RISE deletion error rose from 0.282 to 0.355 and HotpotQA evidence recovery fell from 0.267 to 0.223, compared with an unweighted reasoning span.
lessons.applies_when: Attributing answers through reasoning chains back to context

lessons.approach: Attention-only scoring that omits head-wise value projections
lessons.error_summary: MATH RISE rose from 0.282 to 0.358 and MoreHopQA RISE from 0.112 to 0.140.
lessons.applies_when: Layer-wise attention-flow attribution in decoder-only LLMs

lessons.approach: Continuous cosine target direction instead of a binarized sign vector; more than one recursive hop
lessons.error_summary: Cosine direction was less faithful on MoreHopQA (RISE/MAS 0.124/0.221 vs 0.112/0.182). Extra recursion hops beyond one gave no further gain. Note the per-layer sign variant slightly beat the global one on HotpotQA recovery (0.279 vs 0.267).
lessons.applies_when: Proximity-based attribution in anisotropic hidden spaces

lessons.question: How to attribute long multi-token LLM outputs to context tokens without quadratic cost?
lessons.answer: Aggregate the whole target span into one sign vector of summed final-layer states and propagate it through value projections gated by max(0, alignment), weighting deeper layers more. This runs in one linear-time pass and reports 0.695 evidence recovery on RULER vs 0.635; a single recursive hop through the reasoning span gave the main gain on MATH (MAS 0.489 to 0.365).

title: DynaSpec-RAG: Dynamic Spectral Residual Fusion with Multi-Scale Safety Gating for Zero-Shot Time Series Forecasting
summary: Proposes an output-space module for frozen time-series foundation models that boundary-aligns retrieved analogues, splits them into FFT trend and seasonal bands and gates them per timestep, reporting average MSE 0.1940 to 0.1892 over TS-RAG on seven benchmarks with 0.27M trainable parameters.

lessons.approach: Inject retrieved-analogue corrections at full strength (scale 1.0) without validation calibration
lessons.error_summary: Caused negative transfer on 5 of 7 datasets and raised average test MSE to 0.1942, worse than the 0.1940 baseline; a validation-calibrated global scale gave 0.1892.
lessons.applies_when: Retrieval-augmented zero-shot forecasting on noisy or non-stationary domains

lessons.approach: Insert retrieved horizons at the context mean level without aligning them to the last observed value
lessons.error_summary: Without boundary continuation MSE was 0.2457 vs 0.2433 with it, forfeiting most of the gain over the TS-RAG base (0.2487); alignment also let calibration trust analogues more (ETTh1 scale 0.275 to 0.525).
lessons.applies_when: Blending retrieved future windows into a forecast

lessons.approach: Use only the single nearest retrieved neighbour
lessons.error_summary: Top-1 degraded MSE to 0.1922 vs 0.1891 for content-plus-distance attention over top-k; a simple inverse-distance softmax (0.1890) did as well as learned attention.
lessons.applies_when: Neighbour aggregation in time-series RAG

lessons.question: How to use retrieved historical analogues to improve a frozen time-series foundation model without negative transfer?
lessons.answer: Fuse retrieval as a residual in output space, scaled by a global factor calibrated on validation data so it can never be worse than the baseline there. Low-frequency trend carried most of the benefit (MSE 0.2258 to 0.2205 low-band only, 0.2199 both bands), and the frequency cutoff choice was near-invariant; it also transferred to GIFT-Eval at -5.6% MSE.

title: Neural Mixture-Mode Aligned Merton Jump Diffusion for Continuous-Time Probabilistic Forecasting
summary: Proposes reading point forecasts and samples directly from the Poisson-Gaussian mixture a neural jump-diffusion model already predicts, plus a variance-conservation loss, reporting Mean MAE 17.2 to 14.4 and Best-of-K minMAE 4.83 to 2.89 on S&P 500 and synthetic data.

lessons.approach: Train the neural jump-diffusion at long horizons (28 steps) without an energy-variance regularizer on the predicted parameters
lessons.error_summary: Parameters drifted catastrophically: volatility exploded from 0.016 to 0.071 and jump intensity collapsed toward zero; adding the loss cut 28-step MSE by 46% (13271 to 7162) and raised R2 from 0.327 to 0.637. At 7 steps the loss was roughly neutral.
lessons.applies_when: Long-horizon neural SDE or jump-diffusion forecasting

lessons.approach: Use the mixture mean, or Monte Carlo likelihood selection, as the point forecast
lessons.error_summary: The mean estimator was fragile and degraded sharply on one seed; Monte Carlo selection was 6.3% worse than the analytic median (p-MAE 14.6, spread 0.34).
lessons.applies_when: Point forecasts from heavy-tailed mixture predictive densities

lessons.question: How to get good point forecasts and candidate paths from a model that predicts a mixture density?
lessons.answer: Invert the predicted mixture CDF analytically: use the median as the L1-optimal point estimate and map stratified quantiles through the inverse CDF for candidate paths. Stratified sampling improved Best-of-K minMAE 4.86 to 2.79 (removing it worsened minMAE by 74.4%), with a 2.2x sampling speedup and deterministic results; truncating jumps at 3-5 terms was enough.

title: SPECTRA-HET SPLIT UP: Exact U-Statistic Heteroskedastic Linear-Shrinkage Adaptive GMM for Unpaired Causal Inference
summary: Proposes a GMM estimator for causal effects from unpaired multi-environment data that combines an exact leave-one-out U-statistic cross-moment, heteroskedastic reweighting, linear covariance shrinkage and adaptive Lasso with guarded refitting, reporting up to 8x lower L1 error than standard SPLIT UP.

lessons.approach: Weight environments by inverse residual standard deviation (1/sigma_res) under heteroskedasticity
lessons.error_summary: Degraded severely, up to +1220% error at heterogeneity 1.5, because it ignores sampling variation from the second sample; moment-optimal 1/V weights tracked the oracle.
lessons.applies_when: Two-sample instrumental-variable estimation with heteroskedastic environments

lessons.approach: Spectral thresholding of the instrument moment matrix by a random-matrix eigenvalue cutoff, or no regularization
lessons.error_summary: Unregularized moments were catastrophically ill-conditioned (condition number over 1e10); eigenvalue thresholding over-shrank toward isotropy (L1 error 6.26 at d/m=2 vs 2.41 for linear shrinkage).
lessons.applies_when: High-dimensional moment matrices with aspect ratio d/m between 0.5 and 2

lessons.approach: Naive plug-in or K-fold cross-fitted cross-moments instead of an exact leave-one-out U-statistic
lessons.error_summary: Plug-in stalled from measurement error (L1 1.244 at N=25600); K-fold carried partition noise across seeds; Monte Carlo split averaging was 84x slower (994 vs 11.8 ms).
lessons.applies_when: Unpaired multi-environment causal estimation with many instruments

lessons.question: How to estimate causal effects from unpaired data across environments with hidden confounding and many features?
lessons.answer: Use an exact leave-one-out U-statistic for cross-moments (zero split variance in one pass) and linear shrinkage of the weighting matrix, then adaptive Lasso with a guarded refit. Each part mattered: removing heteroskedastic reweighting cost +36.7% error at N=51200 and disabling the adaptive penalty gave 3.8x more error at N=3200; real-data L1 fell from 20.61 to 11.16.

title: FR-MSH-GGAD: Zero-Shot Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection via Forman-Ricci Curvature and Multi-Scale Hodge Heat-Kernel Diffusion
summary: Proposes adding signed edge curvature and density-gated edge-flow diffusion to a zero-shot generalist graph anomaly detector, reporting +2.12% AUROC and +6.23% AUPRC average over IA-GGAD, with +13.50% AUROC on Facebook and no regressions on sparse citation graphs.

lessons.approach: Use absolute value of edge curvature as an anomaly feature
lessons.error_summary: Folding the positive tail onto the negative tail collapsed consensus AUROC on Weibo from 89.35% to 31.40%, worse than random; 67-87% of structural anomalies sit in the top signed-curvature decile.
lessons.applies_when: Dense-clique fraud anomalies in graphs
