lessons.approach: Apply higher-order edge-flow (1-cycle) diffusion uniformly to all graphs, standalone or ungated
lessons.error_summary: Standalone it was net-negative (-3.05% average) and cut ACM by 17.03%; ungated diffusion degraded ACM by 8.51%; forcing it on ultra-sparse Elliptic lowered AUROC 50.50 to 49.06.
lessons.applies_when: Sparse homophilous graphs such as citation networks and ultra-sparse financial graphs

lessons.approach: Longer diffusion scales (t>=3), and two-tailed curvature scoring that also promotes strongly negative curvature
lessons.error_summary: Scales t>=3 diluted detection by 12.50% on Facebook versus t=1; two-tailed scoring injected false positives, lowering average AUPRC from 42.49 to 39.63-40.88. Source-learned scale projection failed to transfer (82.22%).
lessons.applies_when: Zero-shot transfer of topological anomaly scores

lessons.question: How to add higher-order topology to graph anomaly detection without hurting sparse graphs?
lessons.answer: Gate higher-order operators by global edge density and keep curvature signed. Signed curvature plus clustering formed a regression-free core, and density-gated short-range diffusion unlocked +13.50% AUROC / +34.65% AUPRC on dense social graphs while switching itself off on sparse ones; forced diffusion still scaled to 3.7M nodes in 123 s and 3.2 GB.

title: Tier-Block Orthogonal Contrast Functional ANOVA: Fast, Division-Free, Exact Decompositions for High-Dimensional Categorical Data
summary: Proposes a division-free functional ANOVA for categorical models using orthonormal contrast tier blocks projected away from parent subspaces and block-wise rank-revealing SVD, reporting 100-350x speedups over prior methods and exact reconstruction (R2 = 1.000) on observed supports.

lessons.approach: Block SVD of interaction tiers without projecting away lower-order parent subspaces
lessons.error_summary: Failed catastrophically on CONNECT-4 (R2 = -534203, orthogonality violation 0.439); global SVD matched R2 0.7295 but violated hierarchy (1.64e-2) and used 4.3x more memory (1346 vs 310.5 MB).
lessons.applies_when: Exact hierarchical decompositions over categorical hypergrids

lessons.approach: Inverse-frequency whitening, or centered-mean and one-hot contrast generators
lessons.error_summary: Inverse-frequency scaling upweighted low-frequency noise and degraded reconstruction; centered-mean generators were rank-deficient (condition 6.2e15) and one-hot added 44 collinear main-effect columns.
lessons.applies_when: Categorical fANOVA on sparse empirical supports

lessons.approach: Too strict or too loose SVD rank cutoff
lessons.error_summary: A 1e-12 cutoff admitted near-singular noise (condition 3e12); cutoffs above 0.1 discarded signal (R2 fell to 0.0893 from 0.8156). A wide plateau 1e-9 to 1e-2 worked. Also scales combinatorially at interaction order 4+ with d over 100 without screening.
lessons.applies_when: Rank-revealing SVD in decomposition pipelines

lessons.question: How to compute an exact functional ANOVA decomposition for high-dimensional categorical models fast?
lessons.answer: Avoid dividing by inverse likelihoods: build orthonormal contrast blocks per interaction tier, project out parent subspaces, whiten by the square root of empirical mass, and use one thin SVD per block. It reports 100-350x speedups, high-rank decompositions in under nine seconds, and processing subsets cardinality-first gave the best rank efficiency (R2 0.548 vs at most 0.271 at rank 85).

title: Dynamic Gamma-Poisson Hazard HDP-HMM for Accelerated Observation-Dependent Time Series Segmentation
summary: Proposes modelling state persistence in an HDP-HMM as a Gamma-Poisson survival process with an observation-driven hazard evaluated in closed form, removing the duration cap and reporting 0.917 accuracy on Bee Dance plus a 17.4x speedup and 45x memory reduction over explicit-duration models.

lessons.approach: Add autoregressive hazard memory or attention context to the hazard predictor instead of instantaneous random-feature embeddings
lessons.error_summary: AR hazard memory raised runtime from 893 to 1,114 ms per sweep with no metric gain (NMI 0.549 vs 0.576).
lessons.applies_when: Observation-dependent hazard HMMs

lessons.approach: Freeze hazard rates at segment start (like sampling a duration on state entry)
lessons.error_summary: Boundary F1 fell from 0.574 to 0.528 and accuracy from 0.917 to 0.902 compared with per-frame hazard updates on Bee Dance.
lessons.applies_when: Segmenting regimes whose exit probability changes mid-segment

lessons.approach: Auxiliary geometric transition kernels as in recurrent explicit-duration HDP-HMMs
lessons.error_summary: Mode collapse on synthetic NASCAR: states merged to K = 2.8 on average across 5 seeds (0.613 accuracy) vs 0.964-0.968 and K = 4 with a soft diagonal pseudo-count kernel.
lessons.applies_when: Weak-limit HDP transition kernels

lessons.approach: Report many-to-one accuracy for nonparametric segmenters on high-dimensional neural recordings
lessons.error_summary: Samplers over-segmented C. elegans recordings (K about 10-12 vs 8 labels) and a matched-K KMeans baseline met or beat them, so high accuracy there reflected state inflation, not better segmentation.
lessons.applies_when: Evaluating segmentation when state count is not fixed

lessons.question: How to model state durations in HDP-HMM segmentation without a maximum-duration cap?
lessons.answer: Model stay probability as a survival process with a Gamma-distributed, observation-driven hazard, integrated in closed form, so forward-backward costs O(T L^2) time and O(T L) memory. It reports 17.4x speedup and 45x memory reduction over explicit-duration baselines at T=10000, Dmax=500, and recovered the true K=4 on NASCAR in all seeds.

title: Port-Hamiltonian Dissipative Landing with Conformal Metric Barriers and Randomized Nystrom Projections
summary: Proposes a projection-free constrained manifold sampler using momentum-exchange landing, conformal metric barriers and a randomized low-rank tangent projection, reporting stability at step sizes where landing samplers diverge, up to 5x fewer constraint violations and about 1.9x speedup at d up to 100,002.

lessons.approach: Gradient-based proportional landing drift at large step size (0.01)
lessons.error_summary: Diverged at step 0.01 (0 of 3 seeds stable) due to stiffness, while the momentum-coupled version stayed stable in 3 of 3 with lower violation (0.0418 vs 0.0593 uncoupled).
lessons.applies_when: Langevin sampling on equality-constrained manifolds

lessons.approach: Active-set switching for inequality constraints
lessons.error_summary: Caused severe chattering (0.0571 flips per step) on Two-Lobes; a conformal metric barrier cut it to 0.0006 with zero boundary penetration. A too-wide barrier margin (2.0) also repelled mass inward (W2^2 0.385 vs 0.052 with thin margin).
lessons.applies_when: Sampling near inequality boundaries

lessons.approach: Exact Gram matrix inversion of constraint Jacobians when constraint qualification degrades
lessons.error_summary: Condition number exceeded 1e17 and the sampler diverged on a 100D manifold; rank-truncated randomized projection bounded conditioning and auto-found effective rank 21 at 6.5e-16 projection error.
lessons.applies_when: Redundant or near-singular constraints

lessons.question: How to sample on constrained manifolds at large step sizes and high dimension without projections?
lessons.answer: Use momentum-coupled (Port-Hamiltonian) landing for equality constraints and a rank-truncated randomized projection that filters vanishing singular values. A single stochastic trace probe for curvature cut equality violation about 7x for under 2.5% extra cost, and refreshing inequality Jacobians every 4 steps gave about 1.9x speedup (126 vs 221 s at d=100,002) with violation 0.0029.

title: Exact Kink-Propagated Continuous Piecewise-Linear Dynamic Programming for Static CVaR
summary: Proposes representing the return-augmented value function for static CVaR in MDPs as exact piecewise-linear knot sets with bounded simplification, reporting grid-matching values with up to 35x value-iteration speedup, 43-70x memory compression and zero execution drift.

lessons.approach: Discretize the auxiliary return budget onto a fixed grid and snap to grid nodes during execution
lessons.error_summary: Final budget drift reached 97.5 over 20 steps at grid size 100; even drift-free linear interpolation stayed worse (CVaR -20.02 vs -18.18 on GridWorld100 at alpha 0.30), and at stringent risk the grid drove a sub-optimal give-up budget.
lessons.applies_when: State-augmented static CVaR optimization at tight risk levels

lessons.approach: Continuous optimizers (gradient or simplex) for the outer CVaR budget search over a piecewise-linear function
lessons.error_summary: A quasi-Newton optimizer was 1773x slower than closed-form knot evaluation (0.0494 ms) and was trapped at spurious vertices 80% of the time at alpha 0.60.
lessons.applies_when: Optimizing over piecewise-linear value functions

lessons.approach: Propagate only primary reward kinks; uniform subsampling to cap knot count; no pruning
lessons.error_summary: Dropping secondary kinks gave 10,497x higher error (sup-norm 6.83); uniform subsampling had error 6.92 vs 9.21e-4 for geometry-aware simplification; unpruned functions grew to 5,279 knots by backup 10 vs 65 pruned (39x slower merges).
lessons.applies_when: Exact piecewise-linear dynamic programming

lessons.question: How to optimize static CVaR in an MDP without discretizing the return budget?
lessons.answer: Represent the value function in the budget variable as exact continuous piecewise-linear knot sets and prune with sup-norm curve simplification, which gives a certified error floor of epsilon/(1-gamma). The paper reports matching grid baselines with up to 35x speedup, 43-70x memory compression, sub-0.1 ms closed-form budget extraction, and a divide-and-conquer envelope merge up to 1,449x faster for large action spaces.

title: Sheaf Laplacian Transport Attribution: Cross-Layer Mechanistic Data Attribution via Cellular Sheaf Cohomology
summary: Proposes scoring training samples by how much they distort cross-layer transport on a sheaf built over an induction circuit relative to a token-permuted counterfactual, reporting full-circuit Spearman 0.37 vs -0.03 for loss-gradient mechanistic data attribution across Pythia 14M-160M.

lessons.approach: Loss-gradient mechanistic data attribution on a single component's parameter subspace with cross-entropy curvature
lessons.error_summary: Near-zero or negative ranking fidelity against causal circuit ablation on all but the smallest Pythia model (suite average -0.03 full circuit), and blind when prediction error saturates.
lessons.applies_when: Attributing circuit emergence such as induction heads to training data

lessons.approach: Counterfactuals using random token replacement; adding an energy regularizer to the defect score
lessons.error_summary: Random replacement, which destroys the unigram marginal, collapsed and flipped sign (mean rho down to -0.11 vs 0.388 for full positional permutation); energy weight 1 degraded rho to -0.06 vs 0.262 at weight 0.
lessons.applies_when: Counterfactual design for structural data attribution

lessons.approach: Identity, random-orthogonal or CCA restriction maps instead of fitted ridge maps; whole-network circuit graph
lessons.error_summary: Non-fitted maps collapsed rho to at most 0.22, often negative; using the whole network (0.254) did not beat a compact plus-minus-1-layer subgraph (0.262) at up to 1.4x cost, and a single head (0.168) was too weak. Fidelity also falls with model scale.
lessons.applies_when: Cross-layer circuit attribution in small transformer LMs

lessons.question: How to find which training examples cause an induction-head circuit to form?
lessons.answer: Score samples with a loss-free cross-layer signal: how strongly each sample distorts fitted layer-to-layer transport compared with a positional permutation that keeps token counts but breaks order. It reports Spearman 0.37 vs -0.03 against causal circuit ablation, stays reliable when loss is saturated, and calibration saturates by about 64 samples but needs natural text.

title: Predictive Lead-Lag Integral-Compensated Extragradient for Exact Last-Iterate Convergence in Extensive-Form Games
summary: Proposes an extragradient method with a predictive lead-lag forecast and a harmonic-decay integral anchor for zero-sum extensive-form games, reporting last-iterate NashConv up to 24,000x better than fixed-EMA anchors on Goofspiel 5 (to 1.105e-9).

lessons.approach: Static asymmetric perturbation without integral tracking
lessons.error_summary: On Leduc Poker it failed to converge (NashConv 2.000 at 1e6 iterations, mu=0.1); past the invariance threshold (mu>=0.05 Kuhn, mu>=0.10 Goofspiel 4) prior asymmetric methods plateaued at 0.4131 and 0.4726.
lessons.applies_when: Perturbed saddle-point solvers in sequence-form games

lessons.approach: Fixed exponential-moving-average integral anchor (constant beta)
lessons.error_summary: Left a deep-tree tracking floor (6.977e-3 on Leduc) and degraded sharply with perturbation strength (4.12e-4 at mu 0.001 to 1.85 at mu 1.0); shallow games reached machine precision anyway.
lessons.applies_when: Deep game trees such as Leduc and Goofspiel 5

lessons.question: How to get last-iterate convergence to Nash equilibrium in deep extensive-form games with first-order methods?
lessons.answer: Replace a fixed EMA anchor with a harmonic-decay running-average anchor beta0/(1+kappa t), which turns it into an ever-longer average and removes the tracking floor. On Leduc it reached 8.25e-5 (85x better than fixed EMA), any kappa>0 stabilized all perturbation strengths, and kappa=1e-3 was robust from 12 to 2077 dimensions.

title: Anisotropic Log-Euclidean SPD-Metric Imputation for Tabular Missing Data
summary: Proposes AnisoSPD, an iterative kernel imputer that learns a per-feature diagonal (ARD) metric with a closed-form leave-one-out objective, and reports a mean MAE of 0.320 across 28 UCI configurations, beating the KPI kernel imputer (0.387 reproduced) in 26/28 cases.

lessons.approach: Full SPD metric (matrix exponential of a symmetric matrix) instead of a diagonal metric for kernel imputation
lessons.error_summary: Full SPD gave mean MAE 0.3235 vs 0.3199 for diagonal, at 1.6x the runtime, with NaN failures in 11/28 configurations from eigenvalue blow-up (max eigenvalue about 2.4e9); it helped only on the highest-dimensional dataset (D=41) and overfit small ones (D=23, N=195: 0.307 vs 0.290).
lessons.applies_when: Kernel-regression imputation on small, low-dimensional continuous UCI tables

lessons.approach: Kernel imputer (even with learned anisotropic metric) vs tree imputer MissForest on small continuous tables
lessons.error_summary: MissForest kept the lowest raw reconstruction error on the 7 small continuous UCI tables (0.153 mean MAE vs 0.320 for AnisoSPD); the kernel method only overtook trees on mixed-type, high-dimensional (D>=216) tables and downstream accuracy.
lessons.applies_when: Small, purely continuous, low-dimensional tabular datasets

lessons.approach: Hard complete-case gating of kernel support (only neighbours with observed values, conf_rho=0) and unbounded outer-loop iteration
lessons.error_summary: Hard complete-case gating collapsed under severe missingness, while unweighted support was best; running the fixed-point sweep without early stopping over-smoothed and drifted error upward at missing ratios of 0.6 and above.
lessons.applies_when: Iterative kernel imputation at high missing ratios (p >= 0.5)

lessons.question: How should I learn the distance metric for kernel-based missing-value imputation?
lessons.answer: Use a per-feature diagonal metric parameterized as exp(v) and fit it with a closed-form leave-one-out objective on observed entries rather than an isotropic bandwidth or a full matrix. The paper reports the diagonal metric cut MAE 7.2% vs isotropic (0.320 vs 0.345), winning all 28 configurations, and leave-one-out fitting (MAE 0.300) beat an 80/20 train/val split (0.302) and fixed identity or inverse-variance metrics.

lessons.question: In what order should columns be refined in chained/iterative imputation?
lessons.answer: Refine columns in ascending order of missingness so cleaner features supervise later ones. The paper reports ascending order gave the lowest MAE (0.356, 5/8 wins) vs descending (0.362), random (0.358) and simultaneous Jacobi-style updates (0.363, 0/8 wins).

title: ErtelHodge-STELLA: A 3D Ertel Potential-Vorticity and Baroclinic Thermal-Front Hodge-de Rham Network for Atmospheric Time Series Forecasting
summary: Adds zero-initialized physics-based graph operators (thermal-front edge weights, baroclinic flux, signed diffusion) to a 12k-parameter station forecaster and reports improvement over its STELLA-10k backbone on 10/10 metric-dataset cells and first place on 8/10 among 17 baselines.

lessons.approach: Physics-informed neural ODE forecaster (ClimODE) applied to irregular weather-station networks
lessons.error_summary: ClimODE trailed the lightweight graph model badly (GlobalWind MAE 1.452 vs 1.289; GlobalTemp 3.231 vs 1.915, -40.7%) while using 4.2x more parameters; the paper attributes this to numerical drift from iterative ODE integration over long, irregular spatial jumps.
lessons.applies_when: Station-level atmospheric forecasting on irregular global sensor networks

lessons.approach: Baroclinic energy-conversion flux and physical transport priors on smooth or non-conservative fields
lessons.error_summary: The baroclinic flux was marginally redundant on smooth GlobalTemp, and the physical prior did not help non-conservative PM2.5, so a learned bypass gate had to switch it off; heavyweight Transformers still edged ahead on RMSE for smooth global temperature.
lessons.applies_when: Smooth temperature fields or non-conservative quantities such as air pollutants

lessons.approach: Unsigned (smoothing-only) graph diffusion instead of signed diffusion that can sharpen
lessons.error_summary: Disabling signed diffusion was the largest single ablation loss (+0.34% MAE GlobalTemp, +0.17% GlobalWind); about 62-67% of learned channel coefficients went negative, i.e. the model wanted high-frequency sharpening rather than smoothing.
lessons.applies_when: Graph diffusion over sensor networks with sharp fronts or turbulent fields

lessons.question: How can physics priors be added to a spatio-temporal forecaster without risking regressions?
lessons.answer: Add each physics mechanism behind a zero-initialized gate so the model starts exactly as its backbone and can learn to bypass priors that do not help. The paper reports this kept about 12k N-independent parameters, improved all 10 metric-dataset cells over the backbone, and on 5,672-station WEATHER-5K degraded only 0.06-0.18% MAE when half the stations were removed at test time.

title: Unigram-Calibrated Stationary Discrete Diffusion Language Models
summary: Replaces uniform noise in mixed discrete diffusion language models with an empirical unigram stationary distribution while keeping an exact O(|V|) ELBO, and reports zero-shot average perplexity of 380.7 vs 432.6 for XDLM (a 12.0% gain) from one parameter-free change.

lessons.approach: Smoothing the unigram noise prior with a power below 1 (word2vec-style 0.75) or sharpening it above 1
lessons.error_summary: The raw empirical unigram (exponent 1.0) gave the best perplexity; down-weighting frequent tokens over-flattened the prior toward uniform and hurt density, while exponents above 1 collapsed vocabulary support from 97.5% to 5.3% and also hurt.
lessons.applies_when: Choosing the noise target for non-masked or mixed discrete diffusion language models

lessons.approach: Pure absorbing-mask discrete diffusion (MDLM) scaled from sequence length 128 to 512
lessons.error_summary: Pure masking was best at length 128 but collapsed to worst at length 512 (under a 4k-step budget), whereas the unigram-mixed model's margin over XDLM widened from +8.96 to +20.4 PPL.
lessons.applies_when: Discrete diffusion language model pretraining on OpenWebText at longer sequence lengths and short budgets

lessons.approach: Post-hoc truncation (temperature 0.7, nucleus 0.85, top-k 20) to fix multi-step sampling diversity collapse
lessons.error_summary: Temperature 0.7 lowered sample entropy (2.64 to 2.24) and worsened oracle PPL (402.4 to 417.4); nucleus and top-k left PPL unchanged at 402.4. The paper instead uses a reverse-rate anneal applied only at sampling time.
lessons.applies_when: Long sampling chains (T=1024) with unigram-noise discrete diffusion

lessons.question: What noise distribution should a discrete diffusion language model corrupt tokens toward?
lessons.answer: Corrupt toward the corpus unigram distribution (mixed with masking) instead of uniform random tokens, so noisy states stay closer to natural text. The paper reports OpenWebText validation PPL 146.4 vs 155.3 (XDLM) and 164.2 (UDLM), and a matched-entropy ablation found vocabulary-support preservation, not entropy, drives the gain; a small unigram mixing ratio (0.1) was the best understanding-generation trade-off.

title: Stochastic Delay Differential Flows and RKHS Trajectory Transport for Parallel Inference in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
summary: A training-free parallel sampler for recurrent-depth language models (Huginn-0125, 3.5B) that reports 3.6x-4.3x speedups over autoregressive decoding while recovering full-depth accuracy, and cuts peak CUDA memory from 20.4 GB to 8.2 GB.

lessons.approach: Martingale optimal-stopping (Snell envelope) exit rule for per-token depth in recurrent-depth LLM decoding
lessons.error_summary: Optimal-stopping exit collapsed prematurely: 99% of tokens exited within 32 passes, mostly at depth 8, due to high entropy at chain-of-thought transitions, dropping GSM8K accuracy to 18.5% vs 42.0% for a relative L2-residual threshold. Entropy-gated exit reached only 37.0%.
lessons.applies_when: Adaptive depth/early-exit for looped-transformer reasoning on GSM8K

lessons.approach: Too-tight residual exit threshold (0.01), single inner recurrence step (r0=1), or over-broad RKHS transport kernel
lessons.error_summary: Residual threshold 0.01 ran at 0.004 tokens/s with 12% accuracy; r0=1 collapsed to 0% accuracy from single-step gradient noise; an over-broad transport kernel (1e-4) caused over-smoothing drift and 37.5% vs 42.5% accuracy.
lessons.applies_when: Parallel diffusion-forcing samplers for recurrent-depth LLMs

lessons.approach: Blending KV cache entries across depths with a low-frequency eigenfunction projection instead of overwriting
lessons.error_summary: Keys from adjacent deep passes were nearly identical (cosine 0.9997 at depth >= 28) but initial vs final keys differed (0.3843), so blending mixed in under-converged shallow keys; direct overwrite was kept as default.
lessons.applies_when: KV cache handling across variable unroll depths in looped transformers

lessons.question: How do I pick a robust early-exit criterion for iterative latent refinement in a looped/recurrent-depth LLM?
lessons.answer: Exit on a calibrated relative L2 residual between successive latent states rather than raw norms or optimal-stopping rules. The paper reports a threshold of 0.04 adaptively unrolled tokens to depth 33-64 and recovered 42.0% GSM8K accuracy at 10.7 tokens/s, while entropy-scaled wavefront width cut peak memory 2.5x with accuracy staying in the 38.5-41.5% range.

title: Fed-LanczosSAM: Streaming Krylov Subspace Spectral Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficient Federated Learning
summary: A federated SAM optimizer using a 3-step streaming eigenvector estimate from single-pass gradient differences and a stateless O(d) server control variate, reporting parity with 10 baselines at 25-35% lower per-round compute and 51x less server memory (89.5 MB vs 4,562 MB at N=100).

lessons.approach: Curvature-guided SAM ascent along the top Ritz eigenvector without energy weighting/blending with the gradient
lessons.error_summary: Removing the subspace-energy weighting collapsed best accuracy by 27.11 points on CIFAR-10 (0.4621 vs 0.7332) and doubled the flatness measure (0.0889 vs 0.0477).
lessons.applies_when: Single-pass curvature-based SAM on deep nets in non-IID federated learning (CIFAR-10, beta=0.1)

lessons.approach: Unbounded eigenvalue-scaled SAM perturbation radius
lessons.error_summary: The unbounded radius rule inflated the active radius toward 2x base (0.349) and collapsed to random accuracy (10%) at base radius 0.2, while tanh-damped and fixed radii kept about 61%.
lessons.applies_when: Adaptive perturbation radius in federated SAM at large base radii

lessons.approach: Per-client SCAFFOLD control variates under ultra-sparse client participation; also the stateless replacement on accuracy
lessons.error_summary: With 2% participation (each client seen about once per 50 rounds), SCAFFOLD collapsed to 23.5% from stale client state vs 36.0% for a stateless EMA variate. But in the dense setting, dropping the stateless variate actually raised accuracy by 0.44 points, and the FedWMSAM baseline was 1.65 points higher: a memory-accuracy trade.
lessons.applies_when: Federated learning with very sparse participation (C=2%, beta=0.05) vs dense participation

lessons.question: How can I get SAM-style flat minima in federated learning without double backpropagation or per-client server state?
lessons.answer: Estimate the top Hessian direction from gradient differences already computed (a few streaming Krylov steps) and replace per-client control variates with one global EMA drift vector. The paper reports this matched or exceeded 10 baselines across 12 settings at 25-35% lower per-round compute and cut server memory from O(N*d) to O(d), 51x at N=100.

title: PhySense-AdjointFlow: Direct Endpoint Trajectory Optimization via Differentiable ODE Unrolling for Sparse Physical Sensing
summary: Optimizes sensor placements by backpropagating through the full N-step ODE sampler of a frozen flow-matching field reconstructor instead of a single-step surrogate loss, reporting up to 5.4% lower relative L2 error at 30 sensors on turbulent flow (p < 0.01).

lessons.approach: Backpropagating only through positional keys (detaching observation values) when optimizing sensor coordinates
lessons.error_summary: Keys-only gradients gave relative L2 0.7612, worse than random placement (0.5296), with endpoint loss rising during training (59.6 to 106.3) even though sensors moved 10.2 cells; observation-value gradients alone gave 0.3330 and both together 0.2328.
lessons.applies_when: Gradient-based sensor placement through a differentiable reconstructor on 2D turbulent flow

lessons.approach: Trajectory-aligned sensor placement on a smooth, saturated field (sea surface temperature)
lessons.error_summary: No gain: both placement objectives were statistically identical (<= 0.0002 difference, about 0.043 error) since any well-spread layout captures the variance. The paper also found the released SST optimization never moved sensors because its interpolation detached gradients.
lessons.applies_when: Smooth, low-complexity physical fields where random placement already saturates

lessons.approach: Pure endpoint objective from the start, or constant hybrid weight, and deep unroll depths
lessons.error_summary: A pure-endpoint loss got trapped early when sensors started far from salient features and a constant hybrid weight over-smoothed late fine-tuning; search time grew linearly with unroll depth (4.4 h at N=10, 21.1 h at N=50, 56x single-step) though memory stayed about 14.6 GB.
lessons.applies_when: Placement optimization through unrolled ODE solvers with a frozen DiT reconstructor

lessons.question: How should I optimize sensor placements when reconstruction uses a multi-step generative ODE sampler?
lessons.answer: Optimize placements against the actual N-step endpoint reconstruction error, with a single-step flow loss linearly annealed out as warm-up. With the network frozen and gradient checkpointing, memory stayed about 14.5 GB at any unroll depth; the paper reports 8-9% gains over single-step flow placement that held when test-time step counts differed from the optimized 10 (1 to 50 steps).

title: Doubly Robust Semi-Parametric Schervish Score: Subgroup-Adaptive Clinical Decision Evaluation under Distribution Shift
summary: A clinical decision-utility metric combining doubly robust estimation with shrinkage and a plug-in fallback, subgroup-adaptive prevalence bounds and smooth envelopes, reporting non-inferiority in all 43 subgroup/sample-size cells and 47% average small-sample RMSE reduction on eICU.

lessons.approach: Un-shrunk doubly robust (AIPW-style) transport estimator on small, shift-stressed minority subgroups
lessons.error_summary: Pooled doubly robust estimation suffered transport-bias blow-up on rare-event minority cells (up to -2,566.6% RMSE regression; avg -440.6% for un-shrunk AIPW), and label-shift BBSE left -109.4% residual bias; only falling back to the plug-in mean when estimated bias was high (0.1281 vs 0.0005) repaired it.
lessons.applies_when: Evaluating clinical models on small minority subgroups under joint covariate-label shift (e.g. n=320)

lessons.approach: Using a single global prevalence interval for bounded decision-curve scoring across subgroups
lessons.error_summary: Global bounds produced different subgroup rankings than subgroup-adaptive bounds (Spearman 0.479, 13 pairwise inversions, mean score change 0.037), e.g. African American 0.852 vs 0.946 adaptive.
lessons.applies_when: Fairness or subgroup comparison of clinical decision utility

lessons.question: How do I estimate a subgroup evaluation metric under distribution shift without making small subgroups worse?
lessons.answer: Use a doubly robust estimator with sample-size-dependent shrinkage and a hard fallback to the plug-in estimate when estimated transport bias is high. The paper reports 47% average RMSE reduction on 34 adequately powered cells, worst-case +0.0% inflation across all 43 cells, and cross-fitting is disabled automatically above about 1,000 samples where it no longer helps.

title: Neighborhood-Enriched Multi-Scale Shortest-Path Kernel Networks
summary: Adds a purely linear multi-hop neighborhood feature enrichment to shortest-path graph kernel networks, reporting 10/12 TUDataset wins over HSP-GKN (mean +0.84 points) at a 1.34x parameter ratio.

lessons.approach: Non-linear lifts (gated, norm-scaled) of neighborhood features in a graph kernel network
lessons.error_summary: Non-linear variants were statistically indistinguishable in accuracy (82.87-83.14%) but break scale homogeneity: under rescaled attributes the norm-scaled lift's homogeneity error grew to 999.3 and conditioning to 6.4e15, risking float32 overflow.
lessons.applies_when: Graph kernel networks on unnormalized continuous node attributes

lessons.approach: Unnormalized adjacency or high-pass Laplacian as the diffusion operator; oversized enrichment channels
lessons.error_summary: Raw adjacency diffusion caused feature-norm explosion up to 2.9e10 on REDDIT-B; the Laplacian (81.15%) underperformed even static attributes (81.56%) vs 82.86% for symmetric normalization; channels above 32 inflated parameters up to 1.96x with no gain.
lessons.applies_when: Multi-hop feature diffusion for graph classification on TUDatasets

lessons.approach: Neighborhood enrichment on attribute-sufficient datasets and on an out-of-distribution scaffold split
lessons.error_summary: Enrichment lost on BZR (92.8% vs 93.8%) and IMDB-M (54.5% vs 55.7%) where static attributes suffice, and initially dropped OOD test ROC-AUC on ogbg-molhiv (0.7609) until neighborhood dropout (0.7642) or OGB early stopping closed the gap.
lessons.applies_when: Graph classification where raw node attributes already carry the signal, or scaffold-split molecular graphs

lessons.question: How do I give shortest-path graph kernel networks neighborhood context without breaking stability or speed?
lessons.answer: Concatenate raw attributes with a linear projection of symmetric-normalized multi-hop diffused features, keeping the map linear. The paper reports 2-hop diffusion with a 32-channel cap won 10/12 TUDatasets, concatenation beat residual and convex mixing on 6/6 datasets (82.93% vs 82.27%/82.38%), and linearity lets path features be precomputed so training speed is unchanged.

title: Operator Fixed-Point Shadow Propagation: Single-Solve Dual-Free Differentiation of Convex Optimization Layers
summary: Differentiates convex optimization layers through the fixed point of a smooth primal-dual proximal operator with matrix-free adjoint iterations, reporting exact-KKT hypergradient fidelity (cosine >= 0.9964) with up to 12.9x backward speedups and a flat 899 MB footprint where exact KKT exceeds 29 GB.

lessons.approach: Recovering dual multipliers with an analytical softplus-inverse formula in first-order differentiable convex layers
lessons.error_summary: On inactive constraints the formula takes the log of a negative number, giving 100% NaN backward passes on QP and Sudoku; using raw zero duals without refinement avoided NaNs but dropped hypergradient cosine to 0.83 (QP) and 0.59 (Sudoku).
lessons.applies_when: Differentiating convex QP/LP layers with inequality constraints, some inactive

lessons.approach: Scalar Moreau/proximal regularization to stabilize fixed-point iteration on flat (near-LP) lower levels
lessons.error_summary: On Sudoku, weak or zero regularization gave contraction factor 80.18 and 100% overflow; even a calibrated floor diverged (80.30) because instability came from primal-dual coupling (operator norm 25.3) that a scalar cannot rescale. Diagonal primal-dual preconditioning reached 0.9976.
lessons.applies_when: Non-strongly-convex, near-LP optimization layers

lessons.approach: Matrix-free iterative adjoint on ill-conditioned conic layers, and fixed small adjoint iteration budgets
lessons.error_summary: On SOCP layers the iterative adjoint needed >= 1000 steps (>= 1.6 s) to approach full precision vs a few-ms exact reduced solve (30-50x cheaper); a partially converged adjoint (K in 16-24) had high cosine but residual bias that perturbed Adam into a loss valley.
lessons.applies_when: Second-order cone or ill-conditioned optimization layers trained with Adam

lessons.question: How can I differentiate through a convex optimization layer without factorizing the full KKT system?
lessons.answer: Treat the solution as a fixed point of a smooth primal-dual proximal operator and solve the adjoint fixed point with vector-Jacobian products, stopping on relative residual. The paper reports cosine 0.9953 at 16 iterations and 1.0000 at >= 64, with a residual stop (tolerance 0.05, max 64, about 41 steps) avoiding grid search; ill-conditioned layers should switch to a small exact reduced Jacobian solve.

title: Askey-Decorrelated and Preconditioned Least Squares Variational Inference
summary: Makes least-squares variational inference inversion-free via orthonormal polynomial bases, block preconditioned CG and score control variates, reporting zero small-sample divergences (0/50 vs 10/50 on Pima at N=200), up to 6x lower update variance and about 3x faster steps.

lessons.approach: Diagonal (Jacobi) preconditioning of conjugate gradient for natural-gradient solves
lessons.error_summary: Diagonal preconditioning failed when ill-conditioning came from off-diagonal correlations, needing 511 CG iterations vs 55 for a block-diagonal preconditioner (9.3x fewer).
lessons.applies_when: Fisher systems with strong off-diagonal (mean-covariance) coupling in full-covariance Gaussian VI

lessons.approach: Truncated CG (fixed 20 iterations) for the natural-parameter solve
lessons.error_summary: Truncation gave an artificially better -ELBO (-140.89 vs exact -128.73) from un-converged, over-dispersed covariance (logdet 140.40 vs 111.65); stopping on residual tolerance 1e-8 restored the exact trajectory.
lessons.applies_when: Iterative linear solves inside variational inference updates

lessons.approach: Temporal (EMA) smoothing of target estimates and decorrelation alone without control variates
lessons.error_summary: In the moderate-noise regime (N=1500, m/N=0.82) EMA smoothing roughly doubled median burn-in -ELBO (1533 with EMA 0.5 vs 768 per-batch) due to staleness lag; decorrelation alone did not tame small-N noise. Baseline LSVI and natural gradient diverged at small N (4/20 runs on MNIST).
lessons.applies_when: Least-squares VI with Monte Carlo sample size near or below statistic dimension

lessons.question: How do I keep least-squares / natural-gradient variational inference stable when Monte Carlo samples are fewer than parameters?
lessons.answer: Express sufficient statistics in a basis orthonormal under the current variational family so the Fisher matrix is identity, and add score-function control variates. The paper reports effective condition number exactly 1.0 for any N, reaching the Sonar optimum at N=500 vs N=3000 for baseline LSVI (6x), and block preconditioned CG beat Cholesky at m >= 4096 (35.7 ms vs 263 ms).

title: ScaleMode-NeuralSurv: Multi-Mode Subspace Linearization and Covariate Scale-Tilting for Continuous-Time Bayesian Survival Analysis
summary: Extends a continuous-time Bayesian neural survival model with multiple anchored linearization modes and an unbounded covariate scale-tilt on the hazard, reporting aggregate C-index 0.593 to 0.646 and IPCW Brier 0.209 to 0.194 across eight benchmarks.

lessons.approach: Replacing the bounded sigmoid hazard link with unbounded Softplus to transmit more epistemic variance
lessons.error_summary: Softplus widened bands about 2x (0.553 vs 0.289) but destroyed calibration: IPCW-IBS 0.202 to 0.328, D-calibration p 0.782 to 0.031 (failing), and coverage fell 0.779 to 0.672.
lessons.applies_when: Bayesian neural survival models with hazard modulation links on small cohorts (COLON, GBSG)

lessons.approach: Increasing anchor prior variance or adding output-space functional repulsion to widen multi-mode survival bands
lessons.error_summary: Larger anchor variance raised inter-mode divergence 14.3x yet did not move coverage toward 0.95 because the sigmoid saturates; functional repulsion pushed modes deeper into saturation and shrank bands (0.191). Coverage stayed far below nominal (0.605 overall).
lessons.applies_when: Ensembles/multi-mode linearized BNNs feeding a saturating output link

lessons.approach: Conformal wrappers on a frozen survival model, and learned responsibility-weighted mode pooling
lessons.error_summary: Conformal baselines hit 0.950-0.962 marginal coverage but left risk ranking unchanged (C-index fixed at 0.514); learned pooling weights were nearly flat (0.372 vs 1/3 floor) and gave no gain over simple concatenation (delta C-index -0.004).
lessons.applies_when: Adding uncertainty or aggregation to deep survival models

lessons.question: How can a neural survival model raise hazard above the baseline for high-risk patients without losing calibration?
lessons.answer: Keep the bounded sigmoid for the calibrated posterior and add a separate unbounded exponential covariate tilt on the hazard. The paper reports the tilt was the dominant driver, amplifying hazard up to 24.9x for high-risk subgroups; 3 modes saturated accuracy and coverage at linear cost, and lowering link temperature to 0.5 safely raised coverage to 0.668.

title: Calibrated Hierarchical Value Alignment for Large Language Models
summary: Combines disentangled hierarchical value embeddings, per-value z-score calibration of LLM value scores, and linear extrapolation for extreme values, reporting cross-value embedding overlap cut from 0.404 to 0.119 and significant OpinionQA gains over uncalibrated profiles.

lessons.approach: Steering LLM values to extreme levels (via prompts or latent directions) for steerable alignment
lessons.error_summary: Negative steering cut GSM8K 88.3% to 72.6% and TriviaQA 89.6% to 79.4%; AdvBench refusal fell to 59.8% under negative Security steering and 79.4% under positive Power steering, as low as 51.7% on a finer sweep. Latent Security-direction ablation alone collapsed refusal to 33.1%/14.6% on Qwen2.5-7B/Llama-3-8B.
lessons.applies_when: Value or persona steering of instruction-tuned LLMs at intensity +/-2

lessons.approach: Diagonal-only decorrelation loss on unit-norm value embeddings; hard clamping for out-of-range value scores
lessons.error_summary: The diagonal loss had exactly 0.0000 gradient norm and left entanglement intact; hierarchical contrastive baselines collapsed to near-collinear axes (|cos| up to 0.980); hard clamping saturated 100% of out-of-domain responses.
lessons.applies_when: Learning disentangled value embeddings and scoring extreme value expressions

lessons.approach: Raw (uncalibrated) LLM value-endorsement scores to build demographic value profiles; variance scaling alone
lessons.error_summary: Raw profiling dropped OpinionQA accuracy below the default prompt (53.0% vs 56.6%) because default endorsement bias dominates; variance scaling alone was not significant (p=0.417), whereas mean-centering gave +2.98%.
lessons.applies_when: Persona/value-profile conditioning of LLMs for demographic opinion prediction

lessons.question: How do I correct LLM default endorsement bias when scoring how much a model holds each value?
lessons.answer: Subtract each value's baseline mean score (and optionally z-score) before using scores to build profiles. The paper reports mean-centering drove the gain (+2.98%, p=8.6e-10), restoring profile prediction to 55.5% and reaching parity with multi-LLM Modular Pluralism (60.2 vs 60.3, p=0.942) in a single pass.

title: Violation-Invariant Gradient Normalization for Differentially Private Multi-Class Support Vector Machines
summary: Reweights the multi-class hinge loss derivative so per-sample gradient norm is constant regardless of the number of margin violations before DP clipping, reporting +0.023 mean accuracy over private-SVM baselines and +0.109 from the normalization alone vs standard clipping.

lessons.approach: Standard per-sample global-norm clipping for all-in-one multi-class SVMs under DP-SGD
lessons.error_summary: With m competing-class violations the per-class signal is attenuated by 1/m, delaying boundary formation; removing the invariant normalization cost 0.109 mean accuracy, and competing schemes distorted gradient norms by up to 8.6x.
lessons.applies_when: Differentially private multi-class linear/kernel SVMs, especially many-class data and tight budgets (epsilon <= 1)

lessons.approach: Naive L1 or L2 normalization of the loss derivative to fix multi-violation attenuation
lessons.error_summary: L2 still grew up to 2.2x and L1 under-corrected (0.74x); weights blew up to 1e8-1e10 on well-classified samples so clipping stayed at 100%, and on high-dimensional Cornell (d=4,134, epsilon=4) accuracy collapsed to about 0.724 vs 0.831 for exact invariance.
lessons.applies_when: High-dimensional DP-SGD where clipping injects noise into near-zero-residual directions

lessons.approach: Class-frequency offset for imbalance; extreme fixed hinge smoothing; DP-SGD instead of DP-Adam
lessons.error_summary: The class offset moved minority recall by <= 0.003 (no effect); very sharp (0.05) or very smooth (1.0) curvature lost 2-3 points (0.863/0.862 vs 0.888); DP-SGD reached 0.808 vs 0.867 for DP-Adam.
lessons.applies_when: Tuning private multi-class SVM training on UCI benchmarks

lessons.question: How should per-sample gradients be normalized for differentially private multi-class SVMs?
lessons.answer: Reweight the loss derivative in closed form so each sample's gradient norm is a fixed constant independent of how many classes it violates, before clipping and noising. The paper reports +0.109 mean accuracy over standard clipping, clip rates falling to 8-41% as samples become well classified, and wins or ties in 18/24 settings across epsilon 1-8.

title: Stereographic Spherical-Harmonic Semidefinite Optimization for Robust Mixture Estimation
summary: Maps data onto the unit hypersphere by inverse stereographic projection and solves per-coordinate block-Toeplitz moment SDPs with an energy-distance objective, reporting linear scaling in dimension and 13.5x smaller parameter shift under 3% heavy-tailed noise.

lessons.approach: Raw monomial moment SDPs in unbounded coordinates for mixture estimation
lessons.error_summary: Unbounded monomials gave moment-matrix condition numbers of 1.31e21 and infeasibility at degree >= 4, while the compact spherical map kept max element 1.0 and 11-13 solver iterations.
lessons.applies_when: Moment-SOS hierarchies for mixture fitting at moderate moment degree

lessons.approach: Total-variation or Wasserstein-2 moment formulations with robust (median-of-means) target moments; rank thresholding for component count
lessons.error_summary: Robust moments made the empirical Toeplitz operator indefinite (min eigenvalue -9.1e-3), so TV and W2 constraints became infeasible; W2 needed 1280 MB vs 1.2 MB. Rank thresholding drifted estimated K from 2.97 to 9.94 as tolerance went 1e-1 to 1e-5.
lessons.applies_when: Robust mixture estimation via SDP under heavy-tailed contamination

lessons.approach: Stereographic conformal mapping on raw data with extreme dynamic range
lessons.error_summary: For un-normalized data with norms around 100, the conformal map compresses distant components near the pole, so robust IQR prescaling is required.
lessons.applies_when: Unscaled data with widely separated or far-from-origin components

lessons.question: How can moment-based SDP mixture estimation stay numerically stable and robust to heavy-tailed noise?
lessons.answer: Map data onto a compact sphere first and project robust moment estimates onto the valid moment cone with an energy-distance objective. The paper reports this stayed feasible where TV/W2 did not, roughly halved RMSE at 10% Pareto noise (1.03 vs 3.81), used 66.7% fewer decision variables than TV, and signal-subspace extraction cut the component-count spread 3.8x vs rank thresholding.
